articleTitle: Highway Network-Distribution Network Repair and Restoration Strategy under Typhoon Disaster
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: A repair and restoration strategy that takes into account the coupling of road networks and distribution networks under typhoon disasters is presented in this paper. This paper analyses and quantify the impacts of typhoons on distribution networks and highway road conditions, establishes the coupling relationship between highway networks and distribution networks, and then analyses the energy use of highway infrastructures and the charging and reverse discharge behaviours of electric vehicles; then, it proposes the repair and restoration strategies for distribution networks under typhoons, and build a disaster-resistant highway network-distribution network optimization recovery model, taking into account the synergistic cooperation of multiple resources and the highway network-distribution network coupling model. Finally, the highway network and distribution network of a certain place are selected for actual analysis and calculation, and the recovery results are verified by elasticity indexes.

articleTitle: A Single-stage Bidirectional High-frequency Isolated Converter with An Inverse "Γ" Structure and Its Modulation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In this paper, a novel and efficient Single-phase Single-stage Bidirectional High Frequency Isolation AC-DC Converter (SSBHFIC) is proposed, the DC side adopts a Full-Bridge Converter (FBC), the AC side is only composed of four switching tubes, because its shape is similar to the reverse "Γ", so the following are called Reverse "Γ" Converter (RΓC), and a high-frequency transformer is used to realize electrical isolation and energy transmission between AC and DC sides. This topology has the characteristics of small size, high power density, bidirectional flow of energy, high-frequency electrical isolation, adjustable power factor, and soft switching of all switching tubes. On the basis of this topology, the corresponding modulation strategy is proposed to eliminate the voltage spike in the process of exchanging currents.

articleTitle: Differentiated Pricing Guidance Strategy Based on Electric Vehicle User Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: As the electric vehicle market continues to expand at a rapid pace, the effective management and guidance of users' charging demands has become a significant concern. This paper first analyzes the charging habits of users, divides electric vehicle users into two categories—those with flexible charging behavior and those with fixed charging behavior — and proposes differentiated pricing strategies for these two categories of users. Secondly, a charging load space-time guidance model is established to guide charging users to balance the grid load curve by adjusting the charging time at the time level. At the space level, the charging station selection of charging users is planned to realize the rational utilization of charging facilities and improve user satisfaction. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed differentiated pricing strategy is validated through the analysis of illustrative examples. The results demonstrate that the strategy is capable of markedly reducing the discrepancy between peak and valley loads and enhancing user satisfaction.

articleTitle: Study on the Mechanism of the Influence of Grid-Forming Converters on Series-Compensated Grid Voltage Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The grid-forming converter, as a power electronic device, has the inertia and damping characteristics of a synchronous generator. However, the grid-forming converter is prone to unstable oscillation when connected to a power grid containing series compensation capacitors. This article first establishes a sequence impedance model of a grid-forming converter and a power grid with series compensation capacitors, and analyzes the mechanism of system instability oscillation based on stability criteria using a Bode diagram. Analyze the limitations of traditional methods based on virtual resistors to improve stability. On this basis, a stability improvement method for grid-forming converter based on damping control is proposed. A controller is added to the damping coefficient to effectively suppress the occurrence of system instability oscillation. Compared with the virtual resistance method, the proposed oscillation suppression method has wider grid stabilization adaptability and can be better adapted to changes in grid operation mode. Finally, the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis was verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Dual-channel Feature Extraction and Model Enhancement for Deep Learning-Based Power System Transient Stability Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: This paper aims to address the issues of insufficient feature extraction capability in power system transient stability assessment, as well as poor model generalization capability and robustness when facing various uncertainties and disturbances. Dual-channel feature extraction and model enhancement is proposed for deep learning-based power system TSA. The method uses the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to automatically learn and identify key features, improving the accuracy of feature extraction. It combines the dense connectivity of Densely Connected Convolutional Networks (DenseNets) with the width expansion of Wide Residual Networks (WRN) to enhance the expressive power and computational performance of the model. The ability of the model to generalize and be robust is improved by optimizing the network structure and parameter settings. Tests were conducted based on the IEEE-39 node system, and the experimental results show that the CBAM-DenseNets-WRN model still retains good generalization ability and robustness under different fault scenarios.

articleTitle: A Power Management Circuit with Supercapacitors for Magnetic Field Energy Harvesting System in Power Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: For magnetic energy harvesting systems, power management circuits play a very important role in the system. This paper introduces an energy management circuit for the energy collection system, which can efficiently deposit the collected energy into the load. The energy management circuit is mainly composed of supercapacitor and MCU. The supercapacitor is used as a start-up excitation and energy storage element. A low power MCU is employed to control the synchronous rectifier circuit Three operating modes based on the primary transmission line current are proposed. The system can switch between the three operating modes autonomously. The system is verified through experiments and effectively achieves steady-state operation and efficient energy management.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of Mechanical Stress on the Performance of Transfer Capacitors in Electromagnetic Pulse Simulation Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The transfer capacitor is an essential component in pulse compression circuits, and its capacitance can significantly impact the output pulse waveform. During the transportation and operation of transfer capacitors, changes in their internal mechanical structure may occur, affecting the capacitance of the transfer capacitor and disrupting the operation of the devices. In this research, the variation of capacitance of transfer capacitors under mechanical stress is investigated. The results indicate that under minor stable vibrations, the capacitance of the transfer capacitor remains relatively constant. However, when exposed to impact stress, the capacitance undergoes discernible changes. This phenomenon arises from the influence of impact stress on the mechanical structure of the transfer capacitor, leading to alterations in the distance between the two electrodes of transfer capacitor.

articleTitle: Optimization Model for DS-EV Charging and Discharging Control in PV-ES-DC-FR Park
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Centered around the "PV-ES-DC-FR" park, with the goal of minimizing charging and discharging cost of energy storage systems and electric vehicle, an optimization model for DS-EV charging and discharging control is presented. Considering the uncertainty of electric vehicle charging, an alpha steady-state distribution is used to describe the deviation of electric vehicle charging power. A penalty function is introduced to describe the deviation penalty caused by the uncertainty of EV charging. The goal is to minimize the comprehensive operating cost that takes into account the penalty cost and correct the predicted deviation. In the optimization model, the collaborative control of energy storage system and electric vehicle charging and discharging is considered, and it interacts with flexible loads. At the same time, a carbon trading mechanism is introduced to further optimize DS-EV charging and discharging control.

articleTitle: Research on Mathematical Modeling and Scheduling Methods for Electrolytic Hydrogen Production and Short-Range Energy Storage and Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In this paper, the mathematical model of hydrogen production from alkaline electrolyzed water and storage and transportation is constructed mainly from the point of view of hydrogen production station, and the scheduling method of short-distance storage and transportation is studied. A set of mathematical models covering four modules of hydrogen production, compression, storage and transportation is constructed for the rapidly developing hydrogen energy market demand. The model is based on hydrogen production from lye, compression at 32 MPa, hydrogen storage in type II bottles, and road transportation in 20 MPa long-tube trailers, and the mathematical model is constructed by quantifying the performance indexes of each link using the data of China in 2023. This paper innovatively proposes a storage and transportation strategy that determines whether hydrogen needs to be stored at the source and the number of hydrogen carriers required based on the matching relationship between the hydrogen production rate and the refilling rate of hydrogen carriers. The model is also used to carry out calculations to analyze the configuration scheme of short-haul transportation with transport distance related to the scale of hydrogen production from alkaline electrolytic water.

articleTitle: Adaptive Reclosing Scheme Based on Parameter Identification for Active Detection of DC Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: A true bipolar two-terminal flexible DC distribution network containing hybrid Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) can cause secondary overcurrent inrush to the system when it rejoins on a permanent fault. In this paper, we propose an active-detection adaptive reclosing scheme based on parameter identification, which takes advantage of the flexible and controllable characteristics of hybrid MMC to actively apply an AC disturbance signal to the DC line to be detected by one end MMC after isolation of a single-pole ground fault. The equivalent circuit in the absence of faults consists of line equivalent resistance and inductance linearly, and the equivalent circuit in the case of permanent faults is related to the transition resistance and the location of the fault, which cannot be characterized as a linear relationship between inductance and resistance, and the difference is used to discriminate the nature of the fault. Taking the fault-free circuit as the identification reference model, collecting the voltage and current information on the line side, and the least squares method is used to identify the resistance and inductance parameters of the polar loop. When there is a significant difference between the calculated and actual values of resistance and inductance, it is judged to be a permanent fault. A 10kV DC distribution network model is constructed on the PSCAD/EMTDC platform for simulation verification, and the results show that the proposed scheme in this paper can reliably identify the nature of faults under different transition resistances and fault locations.

articleTitle: An Analysis Method of Influencing Factors of Wideband Oscillations in Fractional Frequency Transmission System for Offshore Wind Power Based on Copula Entropy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the continuous expansion of offshore wind power, the fractional frequency transmission technology has become a competitive means to offshore wind power transmission scheme. However, the dynamic interaction of power electronic devices may lead to the occurrence of wideband oscillation accidents. Clarifying the key influencing factors of wideband oscillation is crucial for the safe and stable operation of the system. The analysis method of wideband oscillation influencing factors based on eigenvalues is limited by the high complexity and detailed parameter acquisition. Copula entropy is a measure of the correlation between random variables, which can quantitatively analyze the correlation between data. It has the advantages of no model assumptions and high accuracy, so it can be used to analyze wideband oscillation data. Therefore, this article proposes a method based on Copula entropy for analyzing the influencing factors of wideband oscillation in fractional frequency transmission system for offshore wind power. The correlation analysis is carried out on the various parameters and wideband oscillation evaluation indicators of the system, and the key influencing factors of wideband oscillation are extracted.

articleTitle: Research on Fire Model and Physical Test of Lithium ion Battery Cabin in Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In order to evaluate the fire suppression effectiveness of the suppression system using in the electrochemical energy storage system, a full-scale fire suppression test platform of the lithium-ion battery energy storage system was established, and key technical parameters such as container structure size, layout of the lithium battery pack, thermal runaway triggering mode, and ignition time were determined. Aiming at the two scenarios of initial thermal runaway and initial physical fire, the standard test methods of fire suppression performance under the two working modes of linkage start test and manual start test are determined, and the solid test is carried out to verify. Through the establishment of fire-extinguishing test platform and standardized test method, the evaluation method of fire suppression effectiveness in electrochemical energy storage system is preliminarily determined, which provides technical support for the revision of relevant standards.

articleTitle: Analysis of Meteorological Causes and Preventive Strategies of Power Insulation Degradation Failures
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In recent years, power companies have dedicated significant efforts towards the construction of resilient power grids. The primary focus has been on ensuring the safety of power grid equipment and cables against severe weather disturbances. However, a less studied but substantial threat to power safety is power insulation degradation, which is not necessarily caused by extreme weather conditions. This paper presents a correlation analysis of 144 related cases of failures to power insulation degradation that occurred in a certain region. These failures are correlated with various meteorological data from the corresponding times and locations and our analysis comprehensively identifies their meteorological causes. The results reveal that insulation degradation is most prevalent in August and September, with peak occurrences daily at 16:00 and 17:00. There is a positive correlation between these failures and both temperature (daily average, daily maximum) and sunlight duration. Further case studies reveal that insulation degradation often results from the combined effects of multiple meteorological elements within different seasonal contexts. Finally, this paper provides meteorological support for the prevention of power insulation degradation failures.

articleTitle: Impact of Subway Power Supply System Failure on Passenger Travel under Extreme Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Under the background of high-speed development of rail transportation, it is of great significance to study the impact of subway power supply system failure on passenger travel under extreme scenarios to ensure the safe and efficient operation of rail transportation. Firstly, the subway network and passenger travel model are established respectively. Subsequently, the impact of the subway power supply system on passenger travel under extreme scenarios is considered, and the affected indicators of passenger travel are proposed. Finally, taking a city subway network as an example, the impact of subway power supply system failure on passenger travel is quantitatively analyzed under extreme scenarios where the subway power supply system suffers from an attack to provide references to guarantee the efficient operation of urban transportation.

articleTitle: Simulation of Smart Interactive Effects of Urban Energy Internet Considering the Price Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The rapid development of "new infrastructure" has opened a new window for the development of urban smart energy, and gradually changed the physical form of urban energy internet, which makes its load characteristics, spatial distribution, and growth mode fundamentally different from that of traditional power grid. Considering the significant impact of the "new infrastructure" on the future pattern of electricity consumption in society, firstly, based on system dynamics, we have constructed an interaction model of "Energy Internet and Electricity Load Storage" for urban energy Internet, and fully mobilized the intelligent and interactive motivation of multiple main bodies, including the new infrastructure, through the price factor. The price factor is used to fully mobilize the intelligent interaction of multiple subjects, including new infrastructure. Secondly, the efficiency assessment model and the best interaction mode of the energy Internet are constructed through the simulation of energy flow between subjects. Finally, based on the system structure, system causal loop and other contents, the smart interaction effect of grid city interconnection is analyzed, and the interactive behavioral decisions of commercial centers, charging stations and residential communities are simulated in different time periods. The results show that the smart interaction strategy can effectively reduce peak load and improve energy utilization efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on MMC-HVDC Oscillation Suppression Characteristics Based on Virtual Synchronous Generator Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: China has abundant wind power resources, and in recent years, the technology and engineering of wind power transmission through MMC-HVDC have emerged in China, such as the Rudong Wind Power Project and the Zhangbei DC Power Grid Project. The oscillation problem between MMC-HVDC and AC systems is a difficult problem to solve perfectly. This article analyses the characteristics of MMC-HVDC using virtual synchronous generator control technology. The parameters of virtual synchronous generator technology are important factors affecting fault traversal and oscillation characteristics, as pointed out in this article. The amplitude frequency and phase frequency characteristics of the virtual synchronous generator are obtained through frequency scanning. Finally, the principles and timing of the oscillation suppression strategy are proposed.

articleTitle: Capacity Ratio Optimization of Thermal Power and Renewable Power in the Northwest of China
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In order to promote the low-carbon transformation of the power system in a northwest region of China, rationally plan the installed capacity of renewable energy, reduce the system cost, and reduce the occurrence of wind and light abandonment, the cost model of the fire-wind, light-water power system was first established. Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) was constructed, and the installed capacity of the system was optimized with the goal of lowest total system cost and maximum renewable energy generation. By verifying the rationality, the research shows that the NSGA-II algorithm applied in this paper is reasonable for the optimization results of thermal power - new energy capacity ratio allocation, thermal power: new energy = 1:1.5; Under the current situation, excessive increase in the proportion of installed capacity of new energy will increase the amount of abandoned wind and light and the system cost, and the cost will increase more when the installed capacity of wind power is large. Considering the flexible transformation of thermal power units and the case of energy storage installation, the proportion of thermal power is reduced to 40%.

articleTitle: Frequency Regulation Strategy Considering User Behavior Uncertainty of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: As the integration of renewable energy accelerates, the challenge of maintaining grid frequency stability becomes increasingly significant. Traditional frequency regulation strategy relies on large generators, which are not adapted to the current conditions due to their slow response time. In recent years, the rapid growth in the number of electric vehicles (EVs) has provided significant frequency regulation potential. However, the inherent uncertainty in user behavior complicates the integration of EVs into frequency regulation frameworks. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing a frequency regulation strategy considering user behavior uncertainty of EVs. Initially, three major uncertainties in user behavior of EVs are modeled. Subsequently, a stochastic optimization model based on chance constraints is established to optimize the participation of EVs in frequency regulation. A particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm enhanced by random simulation techniques is employed to solve the proposed model. Finally, the proposed strategy is tested on a modified IEEE 33-bus test system. The results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively quantifies the uncertainties of user behavior and makes the frequency regulation strategy for EVs more realistic.

articleTitle: Research on Distribution Service Restoration Strategy of AC-DC Hybrid Distribution Network with Distributed Generation Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: As distributed power production equipment and flexible loads become more connected to the distribution system via DC microgrids, the traditional distribution system transforms into a complicated network of AC and DC hybrids. When a failure arises in the AC-DC hybrid distribution network, the system's distributed power sources can be fairly called, and a suitable converter control strategy can be developed to assure the uninterrupted power supply to critical loads. First, a distribution service restoration model of the AC-DC hybrid distribution system is built using the system's unique grid topology and electrical characteristics. The objective function for the proposed model is the lowest power loss load and the lowest system network loss. Then, to increase the suggested model's solution efficiency, an AC and DC unified power flow solution approach is proposed to speed up the solution of the well-known mixed-integer second-order cone programming problem. Finally, the effectiveness of the suggested model was demonstrated in an enhanced AC-DC hybrid power distribution system based on the IEEE33 node network. Research reveals that the suggested model can provide effective distribution service restoration strategies when dealing with system faults, improving the power supply dependability of the hybrid system.

articleTitle: Coordinated Analysis of “Power Quality-economic cost” Based on A Vector Autoregression and Coupling Coordination Degree Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the continuous development of new energy sources, the power system is becoming increasingly complex, and the problems arising from power quality control work are becoming more and more prominent, resulting in huge economic losses. To explore the intrinsic relationship between power quality and economic cost, this paper proposes a coordinated analysis algorithm for "power quality-economic cost" based on a Vector Autoregression and coupling coordination degree method, and selects the power data of a customer area in UK for the example analysis. Simulation results show that the method effectively analyzes the intrinsic connection between the two factors and provides new ideas for the subsequent management of power quality problems.

articleTitle: Study on Damp-heat Aging Characteristics of Epoxy-Silica Material for Switchgear
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: As an integral component of power systems, the reliability and stability of switchgear play a crucial role in ensuring the safety and quality of the power grid. This study aims to investigate the wet aging and thermal aging properties of epoxy-silicon oxide materials utilized in switchgear. Through a series of tests examining surface insulation properties, breakdown strength, and infrared absorption spectrum, the aging process and performance changes of epoxy-silicon oxide materials are explored. Aging parameters were selected using the Pearson correlation coefficient method. The results revealed a significant correlation between the infrared absorption peak of the ether bond and aging time, suggesting it could serve as a key parameter for assessing the aging status of epoxy materials. These findings hold substantial importance in predicting the aging behavior and remaining lifespan of insulated components within switchgear, ultimately enhancing the operational reliability of distribution systems.

articleTitle: Study of Modulation and Power Control Scheme for Three-Port DC/AC Converter for Battery Integrated PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Three-port DC/AC converters, as an efficient alternative to traditional two-stage converters, integrate both Photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage systems, and offer advantages such as high integration and efficiency. However, the asymmetric nature of the DC ports presents significant challenges in the modulation and power control strategy for the converter. This paper investigates a modified control strategy for single-phase three-port full-bridge Active Neutral Point Clamped (ANPC) converters and provides detailed analysis of the modulation technique applicable to this topology. The strategy achieves flexible power distribution by injecting a DC bias into the original reference modulation signal. To confirm the effectiveness of the presented approach, the paper presents simulation analyses and experimental validations.

articleTitle: A New Prediction Paradigm for Nonprofessionals: Prompt-based Zero-code Wind Power Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Reliable and high-quality wind power prediction results are significant for wind energy utilization and power system management. This article delves into the cutting-edge application of Large Language Models (LLMs) in the domain of wind power generation forecasting, leveraging their zero-shot learning capabilities to circumvent conventional computational constraints. Inspired by the success of language-based pre-training models, this study posits a question: Can these models be adapted to address the challenges of wind power generation forecasting? To examine this, we offer a novel methodology for precise wind power generation forecasting that employs prompt-based techniques. This approach involves converting numerical inputs and outputs into prompts, framing the forecasting task as a conversational interaction. Such a method allows for the direct application of language models in the prediction process. Our findings indicate that, compared to conventional wind power forecasting models, the prompt-based approach offers distinct advantages, particularly when it integrates background knowledge with multivariate inputs. This revolutionary method accelerates the modeling process, decreases the obstacles to adopting complex predictive models, and provides new routes for the research and implementation of renewable energy forecasting. Future endeavors will concentrate on enhancing the model's performance and broadening its applicability to other renewable energy forecasting domains.

articleTitle: Capacity Optimization of Wind-Hydrogen Virtual Power Plant Using Thermal Balance Hydrogen Storage Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In China's power system, the proportion of renewable energy continues to rise, yet energy supply stability still faces significant challenges. Energy storage systems have become a key technology in supporting the integration of renewable energy into grid. This paper introduces a Hydrogen Storage System (HSS) that considers thermal balance and establishes a distributed robust optimization model to address the uncertainty of wind power. By implementing a two-stage optimization strategy, the capacity allocation of a Wind-Hydrogen Virtual Power Plant (W-HVPP) is optimized. The system's operational efficiency and practicality are validated using the IEEE 30 bus system. In conducting sensitivity analysis, we explore the impact of wind power forecast error on the capacity allocation of W-HVPP, demonstrating that improving forecast accuracy is crucial for optimizing system allocation. Although this research needs further elaboration, it has provided new design ideas for the design and optimization of W-HVPP.

articleTitle: Adequacy Assessment of Distributed Photovoltaics and Energy Storage in Different Industries
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: This paper evaluates the adequacy of distributed PV and energy storage systems under time-of-use tariff mechanism for different industries by building a two-layer model. It is found that the joint investment of distributed PV and energy storage can reduce the operating cost of the power system and the cost of electricity consumption in various industries. However, due to different electricity demand and cost sensitivities, various industries show different investment preferences. Therefore, the article suggests the development of differentiated electricity pricing policies to optimize energy use and promote sustainable energy development.

articleTitle: Three-Phase PWM Rectifier Control System Design
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The tidal current generator set has the characteristics that the amplitude and frequency of the generated Alternating Current (AC) change with the tidal current velocity in real time, so based on this issue improve the control strategy for three-phase Voltage Source PWM Rectifier (VSR). Introduce the variable exponential convergence law into the voltage outer loop Sliding Mode Control (SMC), and introduce the Phase Locked Loop (PLL) technology into the current inner loop Predictive Current Control (PCC). Build a simulation platform in Matlab/Simulink software, compare and analyze the improved control strategy with the traditional PI control and "SMC+PCC" control, finnally draw the conclusion that it has significant advantages in response speed and anti-interference ability. The result also verifies the feasibility of using this control strategy for three-phase VSR to convert unstable AC power generated by power flow generators into stable Direct Current (DC) power.

articleTitle: An Auxiliary Decision-Making Model through Comprehensive Utilization of Multi-type Active Power Adjustment Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: As the construction of the new power system progresses, the marked increase in the penetration rate of renewable energy, the intensified coupling of multi-energy systems, the closer interconnection among regional power grids, and the accelerated advancement of electricity market reforms have significantly heightened the complexity and uncertainty of the system. These developments pose substantial challenges to the existing dispatching technologies. In this paper, an auxiliary decision-making model through comprehensive utilization of multi-type active power adjustment resources is proposed. Firstly, the paper presents the framework of the auxiliary decision-making model. Then, the paper proceeds meticulously to establish the auxiliary decision-making model, including variables, the objective and constrains. Finally the validity of the model is verified using actual grid data from a specific region.

articleTitle: Optimized Dispatch Techniques for Electric Vehicle Consumption of New Energy Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: This paper discusses the optimal scheduling technology of Electric Vehicles (EVs) in the consumption of new energy generation. In the context of energy transition, EVs, as distributed energy storage resources, have significant advantages for peak shaving and valley filling in the power system. The development of new energy generation, especially distributed Photovoltaic (PV), poses new challenges to grid regulation. This paper proposes a joint optimal dispatch model for EVs and new energy sources based on the summation search algorithm, aiming to improve the level of new energy consumption. The model achieves the optimal scheduling of EV charging stations through the objective function and constraints, and improves the system operation efficiency. Case analysis verifies the effectiveness of the proposed technique and shows that reasonable control of EV charging moments can significantly improve the level of wind power consumption, which is of great significance to achieve the "double carbon" goal.

articleTitle: Hybrid Control Method Used for Class E Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid control scheme is proposed for Class E DC-DC converter, which uses simultaneous modulation of duty cycle and frequency to achieve the expansion of the output power of Class E compared to the traditional control method of fixing the value of duty cycle and modulating the frequency alone. Through the analysis of the formula of each parameter in the Class E resonant converter, the expression of output power about duty cycle and frequency is derived. The comparison of the power range is depicted. Finally, the conclusion is proposed that the hybrid control can extend the output power range.

articleTitle: Research on Collaborative Scheduling Method of Multiple AGVs Based on Electricity Measurement Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the continuous increase in labor costs, using AGV handling to replace traditional manual handling has become a trend. For parallel operations of multiple AGVs, if effective traffic control is not implemented, the operation of AGVs will be chaotic. The existing traffic control methods for parallel operation of multiple AGVs are relatively single, inefficient, and unable to achieve efficient operation and control of multiple AGVs. This article determines the material evaluation value for each AGV device transportation and obtains the priority passage evaluation value through the weight factors of electricity quantity, material type, task type, and waiting time, achieving a more comprehensive setting of AGV priority passage method for multiple parallel operations. It solves the problem of single AGV priority passage setting method for multiple parallel operations in existing technology.

articleTitle: Research on the Output Voltage Sharing Control Strategy of Input-Parallel Output-Series Modular DC/DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In this paper, a distributed control strategy for multi-module Input-Parallel-Output-Serial (IPOS) DC-DC converter system is investigated to address the problem of unsatisfactory voltage homogenisation on the serial output side due to sudden load changes during operation, which affects the normal operation of the system. Based on the double closed-loop control strategy, a virtual DC motor control is introduced to simulate the damping and inertia characteristics of the virtual DC motor and introduce them into the system, so that the IPOS system can achieve voltage sharing on the output side and the total output voltage can remain stable during sudden load changes. The stability and reasonableness of the proposed control strategy are sharing by small-signal modelling and Laws' criterion, and the feasibility of the control strategy and its voltage sharing and sharing effects are simulated and verified on the Matlab/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Voltage Control Optimization for Distribution System Integrated with High-penetration Renewables Considering Voltage Support Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the increase of renewable energy penetration, the flexibility and regulatory control of power systems are facing major challenges. The purpose of this study is to optimize the reactive power control of distribution network under the condition of high permeability of renewable energy. Firstly, this study proposes three evaluation indexes of distribution network-node voltage deviation index, voltage margin support index and reactive power balance margin index. Subsequently, based on the above indicators, a multi-objective optimization model of reactive power in distribution network is established for multi-objective optimization. Finally, the simulation of the adjusted IEEE33 node system verifies the effectiveness and robustness of the optimization model, and proves the adaptability of the model to the real scene and the future power system. By this model, the reactive power control can be accurately adjusted under the condition of high penetration of renewable energy, and the overall voltage stability and reactive power distribution efficiency of the power system can be improved.

articleTitle: Self-attention STGCN-based Interpretability Method for Frequency Stability Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Frequency Stability Prediction (FSP) of power systems is very important for rapidly and accurately formulation of post-fault control measures. However, the traditional data-driven methods fail to effectively incorporate the system spatial–temporal characteristics into the model training, and suffers from insufficient utilization of system information, poor generalization ability in the face of new topology and interpretability. To address these above problems, a FSP prediction method based on self¬attention mechanism and Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (STGCN) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the proposed modified STGCN prediction method utilizes graph convolutional layer to capture the topology of the system to obtain spatial information. Then, the time series data of the system is captured by using a one-dimensional convolutional layer to obtain the temporal information. Finally, through the self-attention mechanism, the node's attention score is obtained according to the active power to perform the interpretability analysis of the modified STGCN model. Test results on a modified New England 39-bus system validate that the effectiveness of the proposed modified STGCN.

articleTitle: Bolstering Electric Furnace Temperature Control: A Comparative Study of PID-Based Metaheuristic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The management of electric furnace temperatures stands as a critical concern across various industrial sectors. Traditional controllers, like the PID controller, struggle to effectively handle variations in parameters and sudden disturbances. This research aims to tackle this challenge by examining the effectiveness of a PID controller enhanced by cutting-edge Metaheuristic Algorithms (MAs) for Electric Furnace Temperature Control (EFTC). Five emerging MAs were utilized to fine-tune the PID controller for the EFTC system, with their effectiveness assessed across five different performance criteria. Five recent and novel MAs were employed to optimize the PID controller for the EFTC system, with the controllers' performances evaluated under five distinct performance metrics. The results indicated that the PID-based NGO emerged as the most efficient optimization strategy, showcasing the shortest rise time (1.419 s), settling time (10.8155 s), peak time (5.1552), and objective value (4.071). These findings imply that the NGO algorithm holds significant potential as an optimization approach for enhancing the performance of EFTC systems in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Dynamic Regulation Strategy of SiC MOSFET Drive Voltage Based on Load Current Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: For the current overshoot problem caused by the high switching speed of SiC MOSFET, in the traditional drive circuit, the drive voltage is reduced to a constant value at a specific stage of the SiC MOSFET turn-on process, and the current overshoot suppression of SiC MOSFET is realized. However, current overshoot suppression and high efficiency are difficult to achieve at the same time when the traditional scheme is applied to different load currents. Based on this, a dynamic regulation strategy of drive voltage based on load current feedback is proposed in this paper. In the specific stage of the SiC MOSFET turn-on process, the drive voltage is dynamically regulated according to the magnitude of the load current to achieve both efficiency and reliability. Firstly, based on the analysis of the transient characteristics of the SiC MOSFET turn-on process, a specific stage of current overshoot suppression by reducing the drive voltage is determined. Secondly, on the premise of ensuring that the peak overshoot current is lower than the safe operating current of SiC MOSFET, the load current range that SiC MOSFET can operate under different drive voltages is obtained. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by simulation model. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional strategy of using 20V drive voltage in the whole turn-on process, when the load current is 60A, 68A and 80A, the current overshoot of SiC MOSFET is reduced by 13.33%, 23.53% and 41.25% respectively, and the loss is only increased by 1.11%, 1.15% and 6.98%. The low electrical stress and low loss of SiC MOSFET is realized by the strategy proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Fault Ride-through Strategy Considering Optical Storage Output in A Weak Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Asymmetrical faults in the grid can lead to a drop in voltage at the Point of Common Coupling (PCC), and in severe cases, there is also a risk of machine cut. The traditional voltage support strategy is easily affected by the unit output and cannot support the PCC voltage flexibly. Therefore, this paper proposes an asymmetric fault ride-through strategy under weak grid considering the power of optical storage. Firstly, the principle of voltage support under asymmetrical faults is analysed, and then based on the allocation of active and reactive currents according to the impedance ratio, the ideal voltage support scheme is derived by taking the operating requirements of grid-connected standards for PCC voltage as the target and the output current amplitude and active power fluctuation amplitude as the constraints. The PCC output scenarios are further classified according to the actual output of the PCC and the ideal active power reference value. When the ideal current reference value cannot satisfy the optimal solution, the optimal current reference value can be solved by associating the voltage support equations and the corresponding constraint equations, and establishing a system of nonlinear equations about each component of the current. Finally, simulation is used to confirm the suggested strategy's efficacy and adaptability.

articleTitle: Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control of LCC-S Compensated Inductive Power Transfer Systems Based on Reduced-order Extended State Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the output voltage of LCC-S compensated Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) system is easily affected by external disturbance and its own parameter disturbance, a Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) strategy based on Reduced-order Extended State Observer (RESO) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a mathematical model is built and the parameter requirements of reactive power compensation are obtained. The relationship between the inverter duty cycle and the output voltage under phase-shift control is derived. Subsequently, the transfer function from duty cycle to output voltage is derived through small signal analysis. Then, combined with the derived transfer function, a LADRC controller using the RESO is designed. Finally, the simulation is conducted in MATLAB/Simulink to verify the correctness of the derived transfer function, and to compare the control effect of using LADRC and PI control under disturbances. The simulation results indicate that the LADRC strategy has better robustness and dynamic regulation ability, which has a broad application prospect.

articleTitle: Research, Design, and Implementation of the Power Market System Based on the Optimization Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Based on the optimization theory of power market, Computational Economics, Experimental Economics, system control theory and the intelligent agent technology, the power market simulation system introduced in this paper has been developed by comprehensive use of various computer technologies like SOA technology, etc. The simulation experiments in the power market were carried out on the power market simulation system. From these experiment results we can conclude that the simulation results can recover the actual power market environment and discover the internal law of the power market. The power market simulation system provides a cheap, effective, reliable, flexible technical platform for the study of the power market.

articleTitle: Influence of Operating Frequency on the Inductance Control Characteristics of Orthogonal Reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: This paper explores the critical role of operating frequency on the inductance control properties of orthogonal reactors, increasingly vital in advanced power systems. These reactors are noted for their compactness and adjustable inductance, proving crucial in high-frequency scenarios like large transformer partial discharge tests. The research begins by developing a mathematical model for inductance quantification and then theoretically examines how frequency variations affect inductance. Through finite element simulations, the study thoroughly assesses how inductance responds to different frequencies, identifying patterns and irregularities that inform innovative design strategies for inductance consistency. The results offer design guidance to improve the reliability of orthogonal reactors across various frequencies. Additionally, the paper considers frequency-induced effects on losses, thermal performance, electromagnetic compatibility, and mechanical stability, promoting an integrated design approach to address these issues.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Control Method to Maximize the Frequency Support Capabilities of Multiple Wind-Storage Integration Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The wind-storage integration systems to participate in Frequency Regulation (FR) is an effective means to solve the problem of the local system frequency stability caused by the distributed wind power connection. However, due to the differentiated power support capabilities caused by different operating conditions of wind-storage stations, the multiple wind-storage integration systems face the challenge of being unable to maximize frequency support capabilities. To solve this challenge, a Hierarchical Control Method (HCM) is proposed for the FR of wind-storage integration systems. In the HCM method, 1) An adaptive FR capability assessment method, which considers the wake effects of Wind Turbines (WTs) and the State of Charge (SOC) of Energy Storage (ES), is proposed to quantify the FR capability of wind-storage stations; 2) A hierarchical FR method that considers the real-time adjustable capability is proposed for multiple wind-storage integration systems to maximize the frequency support capabilities. Numerous test results are analyzed to verify the effectiveness and performance of the proposed HCM method in maximizing FR capabilities.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment for Power Grids with High Percentage of Renewable Penetration for Compound Weather Extremes
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: A mathematical model of power line faults under extreme weather is established by studying the quantitative assessment mechanism of the impact of extreme weather on grid line branches. The ACCF model is used to capture the actual power loss after the random failure of transmission lines in the power system. The normalized grid load-shedding, node voltage, and branch power overrun metrics are used to characterize the multiple fault risk of the grid under extreme weather. The Monte Carlo simulation method is used to simulate the uncertainty of wind and photovoltaic power output and evaluate the risk of node voltage and branch power crossing. An example analysis demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively and accurately assess the operational risk of the grid under different scenarios. This observation can support grid risk professionals in making early warning decisions and carrying out grid risk prevention and control systematically.

articleTitle: Application of Archimedes Optimization Algorithm for Network Reconfiguration to Minimize Power Loss and Voltage Deviation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: An optimal Network Reconfiguration (NR) is presented in this paper using a Chaotic sinusoidal map-based Archimedes Optimization Algorithm (CAOA) to address the issues of poor voltage profile and incurred power loss in the distribution system. The chaotic sinusoidal map was used to improve AOA sluggish and premature convergence. AOA was derived from the law Archimedes principle of physics, which mimics the buoyant force exerted upward on an object, fully or partially immersed in a fluid and proportional to the weight of fluid displaced. The exceptional qualities of AOA are efficiency, simplicity, and robustness. The initialization phase of AOA was improved using the chaotic sinusoidal map to improve the diversity strength of the AOA and obtain a better solution. Searching begins with random acceleration, volume, and densities in the search space. CAOA is applied for optimal NR in power distribution to minimize power loss and Voltage Deviation (VD). The verification of CAOA is tested on the IEEE 30 bus system, and the power loss decreases to 139.365 KW from the base case of 202.68 KW. This has led to a 31.238% reduction. The least voltage magnitude increases to 0.948 p.u using the proposed CAOA from 0.913 p.u of the base case. The base case (before reconfiguration) VD is 0.0035498 p.u and decreased to 0.0013403 p.u after reconfiguration. The result reveals that CAOA is suitable for lowering power loss and VD, thereby improving the bus voltage. The comparison with other methods proves that CAOA is effective in lower power loss and VD. It can be concluded from the simulation that CAOA led to improvement in system distribution performance for quality power supply and reliability.

articleTitle: Research of the Evolution Path of Electricity-Led Carbon Peak Based on the STIRPAT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the introduction of the "dual carbon" targets, carbon reduction actions have become widespread. The electricity sector is a crucial component of carbon reduction efforts. However, the current path to achieving carbon peak in the electricity sector is unclear, and the carbon reduction efforts are relatively small. Therefore, it is necessary to analyze the evolution path of carbon peak in the electricity sector. This paper constructs a power-led carbon peak prediction model based on the expanded STIRPAT model combined with an index system affecting carbon emissions in the context of the electricity sector. It selects the basic data of City A from 2012 to 2021 for fitting, sets multiple scenarios using scenario analysis to predict the carbon peak situation from 2020 to 2035, and proposes targeted strategic suggestions accordingly.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Regional Integrated Energy System Considering Demand Response and Two-Stage Power-to-Gas
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The design of regional integrated energy system can promote coordinated planning, optimal operation, collaborative management, interactive response and complementarity among various heterogeneous energy subsystems. This paper considers incentive demand response and two-stage P2G equipment. Firstly, the cost function of air pollutant control is constructed. Then, the traditional P2G process is decoupled by hydrogen fuel cell to expand the hydrogen energy utilization scene. Finally, in the simulation verification link, the scene generation strategy based on the correlation of wind and solar output and the backward reduction method are used to generate wind and solar scenes, as well as reduce wind and solar scenes to simulate the uncertainty of wind and solar output. A number of scenes are constructed to simulate and analyze the optimal operation of regional integrated energy system. The simulation results of the example established by Matlab show that the proposed strategy can not only reduce the operating cost, but also reduce the carbon emissions and improve the consumption of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Experimental study on fire suppression of lithium ion battery by different extinguishing agents
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The safety problem of lithium-ion batteries has limitation in the application of energy storage technology on a larger scale. It is urgent to carry out experiments to explore the fire characteristics of lithium-ion batteries, and select more suitable fire extinguishing agents for lithium-ion battery energy storage systems. In this paper, the fire experiment of 280 Ah lithium iron phosphate battery was carried out by the way of heat abuse. Perfluorohexanone, sevoflurane and fine water spray fire-extinguish agent with the same dose and storage pressure were selected for fire suppression experiment. Judging from the effect of extinguishing open fire, the time of perfluoro extinguishing open fire is shorter (29 s), while the cooling effect of fine water mist is the best (2.27 ℃/s). From the effect of blocking thermal runaway propagation, the water mist has the longest blocking time interval (2815 s) and the best effect. The experimental research can provide a basis for fire protection design of lithium-ion battery energy storage.

articleTitle: A Multi-objective Optimal Operation Method under Power Allocation for Hydrogen-Electric Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Considering the impact of adaptation of different power fluctuation frequencies of Hydrogen Energy Storage (HES) and Electric Energy Storage (EES) on system lifetime and system efficiency. In this paper, a multi-objective optimal operation method under power allocation for hydrogen-electric hybrid energy storage system is proposed. First, the historical data of renewable power generation are decomposed into components with different frequencies and scales by Complete Ensemble Empirical Modal Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN). The Hilbert transform is applied to identify the mixed energy minima composed of the frequency information under different functions, facilitating the identification of the frequency dividing point for determining the high- and low-frequency power components. Then, the constraints under the multi-objective optimization model containing the system operation and performance degradation rate are constructed with the objective of maximizing the system efficiency and system lifetime. For complex operational optimization, Pareto optimal solutions are obtained using non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-III (NSGA-III). The case study shows that the strategy of H-E HESS proposed in this paper can increase the system energy efficiency by 17.95%, and reduce the degradation rate by 1%. The effectiveness of the strategy is also verified in an experimental platform of an industrial-scale demonstration project.

articleTitle: A Novel Short-term Forecasting Method of EV Charging Load for Vehicle-to-Grid Interaction Strategy Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: A novel short-term Electric Vehicle (EV) forecasting method of charging load for vehicle-to-grid interaction is proposed in this paper. In order to make the charging load forecasting method meet the demand of vehicle-to-grid interaction strategy optimization, the initial short-term forecasting result of charging load is first obtained by the typical data-driven method, and then the dimension of charging load forecasting results is expanded, including the number of electric vehicles connected in the region at each moment and the charging demand time and charging start time of each electric vehicle based on the model-driven method. Finally, the necessary correction work is carried out to ensure the accuracy of the forecasting results. The results show that the proposed method outperforms the traditional load prediction method in terms of prediction accuracy and output information dimensions, and then these additional predicted signals can be used for further vehicle-to-grid interaction strategy identification.

articleTitle: Optimal Defense of Power Grids with Limited Offensive Information
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Deliberate attacks pose a serious threat to the secure operation of power grids. In the process of developing defense schemes, uncertainty in the number of Offensive Resources (OR) and attack strategy are the main challenges faced by the defender. Existing researches mainly focus on the uncertainty of attack strategies given the number of OR. In reality, it is often difficult for defenders to obtain accurate information about OR. This study proposes a modified Defender-Attacker-Defender (DAD) model considering attack and defense costs under uncertainty information of OR to determine the optimal number of Defensive Resources (DR) and the defense scheme. The proposed model is decomposed into two stages and solved by the Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm (C&CG). Case studies are conducted based on the IEEE one-area RTS-1996 system, and the results validate that the proposed method can minimize load shedding when OR information is completely uncertain.

articleTitle: Integrating Photovoltic and Electric Vehicles into Smart Buildings for Optimized Load Management
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Optimization strategy of energy utilization for Vehicle to Building (V2B). In this paper, a detailed study of Building Distributed Photovoltaic (BDPV) energy management system through PV-grid as well as hydrogen electrolyzer is carried out use and reduces net electricity expenditure. For example, according to electric vehicle driving distance, weather conditions. The optimized based-peak demand shift results show using V2B for power generation and photovoltaic power generation is also improves the better economic benefits not only utilization of energy. More revenue can be obtained through V2B photovoltaic transmission than valley power transmission. BDPV-V2B, electrolyzer and fuel cells model can fully cover the power demand of internal building load like deferrable, Non-deferrable, and Thermal Control Load (TCL) in sunny and on cloudy days, there is no extra grid power while photovoltaic power is generated through the grid.

articleTitle: Optimal Capacity Allocation Strategy for Expressway Energy Storage System Based on I-MOEA/D Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the rapid development of the Renewable energy industry, the pressure on power supply in expressway service areas has gradually eased, thereby alleviating the increasing demand for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging. However, the complexity of Renewable energy systems and the impact of a large number of EVs interconnected with the grid (V2G) on the stability of regional power grids cannot be ignored. In order to improve the power quality of expressway service areas, this paper proposes an optimal capacity configuration method for battery energy storage systems, which coordinates and interacts with the main grid, loads, and V2G units. The objective is to minimize the construction and operation costs of the service area Microgrid (MG) and reduce grid fluctuations. Additionally, to address the insufficient diversity issue of the simulated binary crossover operator in Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm based on Decomposition (MOEA/D), this paper proposes an improved method based on adaptive differential evolution operators to accelerate the solving speed of the multi-objective model for capacity configuration optimization. Finally, through simulation verification of actual expressway service area MG instances, the optimal energy storage capacity configuration scheme is obtained, validating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Three-Parameter Asymmetric Optimisation Strategy for Dual Active Full-Bridge DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The efficiency of the dual active bridge converter is determined by the stress on the inductance current. The traditional single-phase shift modulation strategy only adjusts the output voltage, without reducing the current stress, which leads to low efficiency. In this paper, a three-parameter asymmetric duty cycle modulation strategy is introduced to significantly reduce the current stress and improve the efficiency of dual active bridge converters. The principle of three-parameter asymmetric duty cycle modulation is initially explained, and four operating modes are derived based on the relationship of control degrees of freedom. Secondly, the steady-state characteristics of four operating modes are determined through time domain analysis, encompassing inductance current and transmission power. Thirdly, the KKT condition is used to optimize the peak value of inductance current for the three-parameter asymmetric duty cycle modulation strategy, with the aim of maximizing converter efficiency. Finally, the effectiveness of the three-parameter asymmetric duty cycle modulation strategy is validated through Matlab/Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: Power Allocation Control Strategy Based on Microgrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: A control strategy for energy storage systems in off grid microgrids is proposed, which divides energy storage methods based on power critical values, and on this basis, a high-pass filter is used to divide and allocate power to control the hybrid energy storage system. For traditional hybrid energy storage control methods, the joint participation of batteries and supercapacitors in energy storage costs is relatively high. The strategy proposed in this article achieves that supercapacitors avoid participating in energy storage when power fluctuations are small, saving energy storage costs. And by setting the power critical value to determine the energy storage method, the problem of poor voltage stabilization effect of a single battery is solved. A simulation model of photovoltaic microgrid hybrid energy storage system was built in MATLAB/Simulink, and the simulation results showed the effectiveness of the control strategy proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Self-healing Reconfiguration Strategy for Distribution Networks Considering Distributed Generation Output Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: As distributed generation are randomly integrated into distribution networks; their output uncertainty adversely affects self-healing reconfiguration. This paper proposes a self-healing reconfiguration strategy for distribution networks that considers the uncertainty of distributed generation output. After the fault occurs, the output of photovoltaic and wind turbine is modeled, and the time-varying characteristics of load are also considered. Then, the objective function is to maximize the recovery coefficient of important load, minimize network loss, voltage deviation, and switching action times. The multi-objective optimization approach is employed to construct the self-healing reconfiguration model, which is solved using an improved genetic algorithm. Finally, the IEEE 33-bus distribution system is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Efficient Harmonic Current Mitigation in Unbalanced, Nonlinear Loads Using Grid-Connected Three Phase Four Wire Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Currently, there is a significant level of energy consumption stemming from nonlinear loads. These loads serve as the origin of current harmonics, which consequently infiltrate the power grid, leading to waveform alterations in the source and a decline in its overall quality. The primary aim of this study is to mitigate the impact of harmonics by restoring the current to a sinusoidal form. To achieve this objective, an electrical system will be modeled using the Simulink software. Within this system, an active power filter comprising three levels and four parallel wires will be implemented. The control methodology for the filter's development is based on the multiple synchronous frame technique. A harmonic current extraction method that employs a multiple synchronous frame technique to generate precise reference currents with reduced computational overhead and a control strategy for the APF have been developed to enhance performance under nonlinear, balanced, and unbalanced load situations. The proposed method significantly enhances harmonic current extraction performance and reduce Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) to acceptable levels and minimize excessive neutral currents. The superiority and accuracy of the proposed algorithms are proved by mathematical analysis and Matlab Simulink simulations.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and System Parameter Sensitivity Analysis of PEMEL Hydrogen Production System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Electrolyzer (PEMEL) hydrogen production system has significant advantages in the utilization of renewable energy for hydrogen production due to its high efficiency and wide operating range. In this study, we present a new approach for dynamic modeling and multivariate parameter sensitivity analysis of a coupled electric reactor-auxiliary engine PEMEL hydrogen production system. We considered factors such as temperature, pressure and water supply and modeled the dynamic material and energy balances for the electric reactor and auxiliary engine, respectively. We verified the system output characteristics and employed two sensitivity analysis methods, Taguchi analysis and analysis of variance (ANOVA). By constructing orthogonal arrays and signal-to-noise ratio analysis, we determined the contributions of different parameters to the key system metrics and the optimal operating combinations. The experimental results show that the system power is most affected by pressure, followed by temperature and water supply. Pressure has the highest contribution of 77.98%. Temperature is the second effective parameter with a contribution ratio of 16.16%. In contrast, water supply has little effect on the performance of the hydrogen production system in the electrolyzer.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Configuration of Hybrid Energy Storage Capacity in Small Hydro-photovoltaic-storage Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In order to reduce the construction and operation costs of hybrid energy storage systems in Hydro-Photovoltaic-Storage Microgrid, a capacity optimization model for hybrid energy storage is studied. Firstly, based on the static model of the entire lifecycle cost, with the objective function of minimizing the total cost and considering the power supply reliability of the microgrid, the load shortage rate of the microgrid system is selected as the constraint of the optimization problem, and a hybrid energy storage system capacity optimization configuration model is established. Next, consider the issue of battery lifespan and optimize the charging and discharging strategies for batteries and supercapacitors. Finally, the improved learning factor particle swarm optimization algorithm and sparrow search algorithm were used to solve the model. Based on MATLAB, simulation analysis was conducted on two examples, and the results showed that the sparrow search algorithm obtained lower full lifecycle costs and faster convergence speed.

articleTitle: Transient Characteristics of Transmission Line Lightning Stroke based on ATP-EMTP
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In order to study the transient distribution characteristics of transmission line when two-phase grounding short-circuit accident occurs on transmission line when lightning strikes, the electromagnetic transient calculation model of 220kV transmission line with length of 32.2km and including 47 towers is established in ATP-EMTP software. The fault type of two-phase grounding short-circuit occurred when the line is struck by lightning is simulated and calculated. The calculation results show that the transmission line has been damaged by lightning When the number of towers on both sides of the fault point is almost the same, the over-voltage distribution on both sides is basically symmetrical distribution, but when the fault point is close to one end of the line This conclusion can provide a theoretical basis for differential lightning protection of transmission lines.

articleTitle: Research on the Structure and Control of A Novel Automatic Voltage Flow Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The Step Voltage Regulator (SVR) has been utilized in distribution systems for several decades. However, the rapid development of renewable energy and distributed generation has imposed limitations on the regulation performance and lifespan of traditional SVR due to voltage instability caused by high renewable energy penetration. Additionally, the stepwise voltage adjustment inherent to SVR cannot ensure precise voltage regulation. Furthermore, SVR is incapable of providing reactive power support or compensating for three-phase imbalance. This paper proposes a solution that integrates power electronic devices with SVR. By incorporating a Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) proportional to the voltage regulation range, the adjustment range of traditional SVR is increased by more than 20%, while also providing three-phase imbalance compensation and reactive power support. A 10kV 2MVA model is designed, and the control strategy and effectiveness of this solution are validated through simulations using Simulink.

articleTitle: Short-Term User Load Forecasting Method Considering Meteorological Factors Based on Conv1D-LSTM with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the energy system transition to more intellectualized, more flexible and more interactive, power companies need more accurate load forecasting results to design effective dispatching and operation schemes to improve competitive in market. Load forecasting, especially short-term load forecasting for a single power user, plays an increasingly important role in power grid planning and stable operation in the future. A Conv1D-LSTM neural network model based on attention mechanism is established in this paper, considers a time of the day index, a day of the week index and seasonal factors, which is shown to increase the forecasting accuracy, so as to avoid the negative impact of environmental variables. The experimental results show that the Conv1D-LSTM neural network model based on attention mechanism can absorb the advantages of CNN network automatic feature extraction and LSTM network efficient processing of time series, and improve the prediction accuracy. Moreover, in order to evaluate the performance of the model in this paper, the performance of the other machines, namely a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) is also shown. The results show that this model can reduce the generalization error of the model, it is verified that the method based on Conv1D-LSTM with attention mechanism can faster model training speed, higher prediction accuracy and lower prediction error.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling Operation Strategy of AC-DC Hybrid Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the integration of a high proportion of renewable energy, the power system's supply-side volatility and randomness intensify, highlighting the dual contradiction between renewable energy curtailment and the system's power supply capability. The participation of flexible resources from sources, loads, and storage in dispatch is crucial for ensuring power supply reliability and renewable energy integration. Currently, the dispatch automation system uses relational databases, which struggle to meet the demands for fast computation. Therefore, this paper proposes an optimal dispatch strategy for AC/DC hybrid distribution networks based on graph computation. First, it utilizes a graph database to integrate spatiotemporal data from sources, networks, loads, and storage. Second, it establishes a 24-hour sequential optimal dispatch model for flexible resources based on the definitions of generalized load and generalized energy storage, considering both supply guarantee and integration goals. Finally, a fast power flow calculation method based on graph computation is proposed to verify whether the optimization results meet dispatch operation safety requirements. Results that do not meet operational requirements are recalculated by adding corresponding operational constraints. A simulation analysis is then conducted based on AC/DC hybrid distribution network data with integrated flexible resources. The results show that integrating generalized load and generalized energy storage can improve the economic efficiency of power system dispatch, reducing power shortage rates and curtailment rates.

articleTitle: Research on Phase Angle Differential Protection Method for Distribution Network with Photovoltaic Access
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Photovoltaic grid-connected changes the power flow distribution of the traditional distribution network, and the fault characteristics of the distribution network will also change, resulting in the traditional phase Angle differential protection method is no longer applicable. Therefore, it is necessary to study a new method of phase Angle differential protection in distribution network. In this paper, the principle of low voltage traverse control strategy of PV is analyzed, and the output characteristics of PV during failure are obtained.
