However, this also causes voltage violations in the distribution network during periods of low/high PV generation, resulting in excessively low/high voltages. Existing Static Var Compensator (SVC) devices cannot meet the voltage regulation demands. This paper investigates the control mechanism of energy storage converters in addressing voltage limit violations in distribution networks with high PV penetration, leveraging the fast reactive power regulation characteristics of energy storage converters. Based on this, explore the reactive power regulation capability of the energy storage converters, construct reactive power regulation modes and a model for the energy storage converter, solve it, and finally propose methods to enhance the reactive power regulation capability of the energy storage converters. The results of case studies demonstrate that the proposed method effectively addresses voltage limit violations in the distribution network and improves voltage quality in distribution networks with high distributed PV penetration.

articleTitle: Research on Bi-level Optimal Dispatching of Hydro-solar-energy Storage Complementary System and Thermal Power Unit based on Underwater Compressed Air Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The power dispatching of a hydropower station in northwest China is affected by water conservancy dispatching, which leads to the limited power dispatching flexibility of the Hydro-Solar Complementary System (HSCS). In this paper, the coupling of hydropower station and Underwater Compressed Air Energy Storage (UW-CAES) is proposed to improve the peaking capacity of the whole complementary system. Firstly, the design scheme of Hydro-Solar-Energy Storage Complementary System (HSESCS) based on UW-CAES is proposed. Secondly, in order to ensure the coordinated operation of HSESCS and thermal power units, a bi-level optimal dispatching model is established, which takes the minimum variance of net load and the maximum output of HSESCS as the upper objective function and the minimum total operating cost as the lower objective function. Finally, the validity of the proposed model is verified by comparing the three models under typical daily scenarios. The results show that the bi-level optimal dispatching strategy can obviously suppress the power fluctuation of net load, reduce the peak load pressure of thermal power units, ensure the safe and stable operation of the system, and reduce the total operating cost. UW-CAES can effectively reduce the curtailed power of hydropower station during the flood discharge period, increase the proportion of clean energy and further reduce the total operating cost of the system.

articleTitle: Real-time Scheduling of Renewable Energy Considering Uncertainty of Renewable Power Forecasts Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The intermittency and uncertainty nature of the renewable energy generation has posed great challenges to the real-time generation scheduling. Traditional optimization methods are hard to meet the requirement of computation accuracy and speed simultaneously. To address these challenges, this paper proposed novel real-time scheduling schemes using deep reinforcement learning. Specially, an open-source platform named Scheduling of renewable Energy with Deep Reinforcement Learning (SEDRL) combining PandaPower, OpenAI Gym and Stable-Baselines has been designed to help create benchmark cases of power system real-time scheduling and operation. Case studies have demonstrated excellent performance of the proposed schemes and scalability of the open-source platform.

articleTitle: Active Support Technology for Wind Farm Frequency and Voltage Based on Hybrid Ultracapacitor Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Wind farms are generally constructed in more remote areas with long electrical distances from power centers, resulting in relatively low short circuit ratios of wind farms, and the station side of the wind farm reflects the characteristics of a weak grid. In a weak grid scenario, when wind power is large, the system tends to oscillate, which in severe cases leads to off-grid wind turbines and large amounts of wind abandonment resulting in economic losses. In order to improve the grid-connected strength of wind farms, it is necessary to enhance the active support capability of wind farms. The use of battery energy storage systems to enhance the grid-connected strength of wind farms is an effective way, but the large-scale application in this scenario is limited due to the limited number of battery cycles and unsuitable for large-multiplication charging and discharging. The aim of this paper is to study the hybrid ultracapacitor energy storage system with high power density, energy density and high cycle times, and to consider inertia support, primary frequency regulation as well as voltage regulation strategies, to comprehensively enhance the grid-connection strength of wind farm stations under a weak grid, to shorten the equivalent electrical distance of wind farms, and to improve the stability of the system.

articleTitle: Research On Compound Differential Protection Method of Symmetrical Dual-core Phase Shifting Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The symmetrical dual core phase shifting transformer, a critical power flow control device, facilitates dynamic transmission power adjustment, enhancing grid flexibility. However, its intricate wiring configuration and internal structure lead to a complex topology, posing challenges in designing effective body protection. To address this issue, this study employs fundamental principles like Kirchhoff's current law and electromagnetic induction to develop a compound differential protection scheme for the symmetrical dual-core transformer. The proposed scheme incorporates a single relay setup that can detect turn-to-turn and ground faults in series transformers, excitation transformers, as well as line short circuits, thereby simplifying the protection configuration. To validate the scheme's feasibility and efficacy, a MATLAB/Simulink model of the transformer was created, and extensive simulations were conducted.

articleTitle: Decentralized Coordinated Control Strategy for Transient Voltage in Renewable Energy Stations Based on Grid-forming Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Transient voltage security and stability of high proportional renewable energy grid requires renewable energy station to have strong active transient voltage support capability. The voltage source characteristic of grid-forming converters is the key to improve the transient voltage control ability of renewable energy station. This paper proposes a decentralized coordinated control strategy for transient voltage in renewable energy stations based on grid-forming converters. Firstly, based on multiple reactive sources control characteristics, the influence of internal voltage on transient voltage is analyzed, and active support system for transient voltage of multiple reactive sources is improved. Grid-forming converters are used as the internal voltage of the station to ensure fast reactive power compensation ability of grid-following converters and SVG, and the compensation capacity is supplemented by SVC. Secondly, transient control strategy is improved. Transient voltage compensation strategy of grid-forming converter / SVG, transient reactive power compensation strategy of grid-following converter and transient switching control strategy of SVC are proposed to realize active support of the whole process during transient voltage condition. Finally, a typical scenario of transient low voltage active support under weak grid is established. The effectiveness and practicability of the proposed transient voltage decentralized cooperative control strategy are analyzed and verified.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on High Weight Features Values in Different Electricity Spot Markets Involving Energy Storage Participation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the increase in installed capacity of electrochemical energy storage and new energy, the spot electricity market is booming in multiple provinces across the country. However, for the new type of electrochemical energy storage, the trading rules of electricity spot market are diverse and complex. Therefore, this article focuses on electrochemical energy storage as a market participant and aims at interpreting the revised trading rules of the electricity market in Shandong and the latest compilation of electricity market rules in Shanxi Province. It is found that there are multiple similarities in the trading rules of the spot market in the two provinces. In addition, the spot market is one of the main profit points for electrochemical energy storage stations, and the accuracy of predicting the clearing electricity price in the spot market will directly affect its profit situation. So, by classifying and analyzing the market disclosure data of two provinces in the past year, this study analyzes the impact of predicting the total output of new energy and predicting the bidding space of units on the daily clearing electricity price. And based on the analysis results of the classification model, guidance and recommendations were provided on how electrochemical energy storage can optimize quantity and price bidding strategies in the spot market.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-based Distribution Network Parameters Adaptive Electric Vehicle Load Forecasting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are developing at a rapid pace, and this has a substantial influence on the distribution network due to their increasing charging demands. The paper proposes a reinforcement learning-based parameter adaptive combination prediction method for the spatiotemporal distribution prediction problem of EV charging load. Taking into account the characteristics of randomness and intermittency in the charging load of ultra-fast charging stations, this study initially analyzes a variety of factors influencing the EV charging load, including vehicle types, driving characteristics, and charging modes, and explores the load characteristics of electric vehicles. Secondly, a parameter adaptive combination prediction model is presented that combines multiple prediction methods. It makes use of the Q-learning algorithm in reinforcement learning to dynamically modify the weights of various prediction methods based on the prediction error, thereby increasing the prediction accuracy. Finally, an analysis of the IEEE 33-node distribution network case confirms the efficacy of the suggested method. This method can accurately anticipate load for EV charging station planning and grid operation, according to the results, which helps to maximize resource allocation and improve grid operating efficiency.

articleTitle: Stochastic Optimization of Pricing Strategy for Electricity Retailers Based on One-Leader-Many-Follower Game
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: To improve the revenue of electricity retailers, a stochastic optimization pricing strategy considering the uncertainty of photovoltaic-storage users is proposed. Firstly, considering the initiative and decision-making ability of the retailer-load-storage triad, with the retailer as the leader and the load and storage as followers, a one-leader-many-follower game model between the retailer and multiple photovoltaic-storage users is established. Secondly, considering the uncertainty of user-side load forecasting and photovoltaic output, typical scenarios are generated based on the cumulative distribution function clustering of prediction error. Finally, a neural network agent model is used to fit the purchasing and selling behavior of photovoltaic-storage users to electricity retailers, replacing the decision-making process of storage output and the demand response behavior of loads. The genetic algorithm is used for iterative optimization and the neural network agent model is corrected, continuously updating the internal pricing of the retailer. The effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm is verified through a test system containing four photovoltaicstorage users, increasing the expected revenue of retailers considering the impact of uncertainty factors, and avoiding the complex invocation of lower-level optimization models, saving computation time.

articleTitle: Twin GRU Model Considering Spatial-Temporal Correlation is Used for Ultra-short-term Wind Power Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The spatiotemporal characteristics of wind power data play a crucial role in the prediction of wind power generation. However, current methodologies for wind power forecasting primarily focus on the temporal variations of wind speed and power, neglecting the spatial and temporal correlations among turbines within the same wind farm. This leads to suboptimal information utilization and insufficient predictive accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a novel twin GRU model that accounts for spatiotemporal correlations which applied to ultra-short-term wind power forecasting. Specifically, centered on the target turbine, a wind shift model is established based on wind direction to delineate the wind shift range. Subsequently, turbines with high correlation within each wind shift range are dynamically selected based on time warping correlation, forming a comprehensive turbine array that provides advanced wind speed and power reference data for the target turbine. Moreover, considering the temporal nature of wind speed and power data, the twin GRU model is designed to extract the temporal correlations within the wind speed and power of the turbine array. Simulation evaluation using actual data from a wind farm in Northwest China demonstrates that this method outperforms conventional forecasting models.

articleTitle: A Transformer-based Long-term Prediction Model for Charging Pile Power Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The distribution, quantity, and charging speed of charging piles have a direct impact on the popularity of electric vehicles, which has been a topic of widespread concern in recent years. By predicting the power consumption of charging piles, the operation and energy utilisation efficiency of charging piles can be optimised, thereby aiding in the layout and management of charging infrastructure. Consequently, this paper concentrates on the long-term sequence prediction of charging pile power consumption. The field of time series prediction has witnessed considerable advancement with the advent of deep learning. However, the majority of studies have concentrated on the analysis of complete data, with intermittent time series prediction receiving comparatively limited attention. In order to enhance the prediction of the power consumption of charging piles with intermittent characteristics, a novel model is developed. This model is based on the Transformer architecture and employs separate inputs for position and value during the input process. Within the model, modules with time segmentation and fusion are selected to replace the attention mechanism of general Transformer-like models. Finally, Split-Attention with mixed values and positions is employed, and information fusion is performed at the conclusion of the model. The experiments are conducted on a real dataset, utilising common evaluation metrics for time series prediction and metrics that have been demonstrated to be more suitable for intermittent time series. The experimental results demonstrate that the model is more effective than several commonly used time series prediction baselines in predicting the power consumption of charging piles.

articleTitle: Balancing Control for Energy Storage Clusters Based on Cooperative Output Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: This paper investigates a distributed cooperative control strategy for large-scale heterogeneous energy storage devices aggregated to form a Virtual Storage Plant (VSP) that behaves in a similar fashion as centralized storage stations in terms of capacity and dynamic response capabilities. Similar to conventional energy storage facilities, maintaining a balanced state of charge is a critical goal for energy management within a VSP. Taking into account the dynamic models of energy storage systems and converters, we propose a synthesis method for designing homogeneous virtual external systems and output regulators within a multi-agent system framework. This approach enables the generation and tracking of consistent reference trajectories, ensuring that the VSP maintains a uniform internal state of charge while responding to external power commands. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is validated through Simulink simulation tests and further verified on a distributed control test platform set up in a real network environment.

articleTitle: Operation Mode Extraction for Frequency Stability Control of Power Systems Based on Improved Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Under the background of large-scale integration of renewable energy and the rapid development of HVDC transmission systems, the power system shows the trend of low inertia characteristic and the over-frequency stability risk threatens the safe operation of power system. The traditional method of formulating frequency control strategy based on a limited pre-set operation modes could not meet the requirements of sufficiency and security for safe and stable operation of the power system. Therefore, this paper proposes an operation mode extraction algorithm based on the improved density clustering algorithm and K-Means++ algorithm. A density clustering based on correlation coefficient is first used to divide power grid output scenarios. Then, based on the result of scenario division, the improved K-Means ++ algorithm is used to obtain the typical daily operation modes. Finally, the validity and rationality of the proposed algorithm in extracting operation mode and analyzing frequency stability are verified by a practical case study.

articleTitle: Quantitative Method Based on Converter-Aggregation-Generation Station Collaboration for Evaluating Suppression Effectiveness of DC Blocking Fault-Induced Transient Overvoltage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In areas with abundant new energy, an effective way for energy utilization is to converge the power generated by a large number of new energy power generation stations and then transmit it through HVDC (High Voltage Direct Current) lines. However, when DC blocking faults occur in traditional HVDC system, it often leads to severe transient overvoltage on the AC side of the system, gives rise to the need for dynamic reactive power sources in suppressing transient overvoltage, and there is an urgent need for quantifying the effectiveness of dynamic reactive power sources in suppressing transient overvoltage. This paper first analyzes the characteristics of DC blocking faults and the transient overvoltage conduction characteristics between converter stations, aggregation stations, and new energy generation stations. Secondly, based on the quantification of overvoltage severity at one individual station, a multi-site collaborative DC blocking transient overvoltage severity index considering voltage amplitude and change rate is proposed. Based on this index, a quantitative method for suppression effective of DC blocking transient overvoltage based on the collaboration between converter stations, aggregation stations and generation stations is developed. Then, the effectiveness of this method was verified through time-domain simulation analysis. The quantitative results provide reference basis for the study of characteristics of dynamic reactive power compensation equipment, planning site selection, scheduling decisions, and other aspects.

articleTitle: Research on Improved Design Method of Phase-locked Loop for Inter-harmonic Interference Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Phase Locked Loop (PLL) based on double second-order generalized integrator is widely used in grid-connected inverters to realize grid voltage synchronization and harmonic/inter-harmonics filtering. However, when there are persistent voltage harmonics/inter-harmonics in the low frequency range in weak power systems, the filtering effect of the PLL is not satisfactory. Especially when the number and frequency of harmonics/inter-harmonics in the low frequency range are dynamic, the filtering effect is further reduced. Therefore, an improved design method for PLL in weak power systems is proposed in this paper. In the improved structure of the PLL, an adaptive wide-frequency disturbance suppression module is added to improve the ability of the PLL to suppress the continuous dynamic wide-frequency disturbance signals and to improve the accuracy of extracting the synchronization signals of the grid voltage in weak power systems. The simulation research in MATLAB/Simulink shows the method proposed in this paper can filter out the DC component and the specified intermittent component adaptively, which provides technical support for guaranteeing efficient and high-quality energy transmission between the inverter and the grid, as well as improving the stability of the grid.

articleTitle: Thermal Modeling and Control for A Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis (PEMWE) System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Temperature control is crucial for the safety and efficiency of the Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis (PEMWE) system during continuous operation. This paper focuses on modeling the thermal behavior and designing temperature controllers for a PEMWE system operating under dynamic conditions. A dynamic thermal model of the PEMWE system is developed for simulation and controller design, and its effectiveness is validated using a hardware-in-the-loop simulation platform and real experimental data. Based on this model, an optimized fuzzy PID controller is designed to minimize temperature overshoot. Experimental results indicate that the optimized fuzzy PID controller, compared to traditional PID control, reduces the pump regulation time by approximately 70 seconds and decreases the overshoot by around 4%, resulting in improved control effectiveness. Ultimately, the temperature difference between the electrolyzer inlet and outlet is fine-tuned, the impact of various temperature differences on the PEMWE system is evaluated, and it is recommended to regulate the temperature difference to 3-5°C.

articleTitle: An Improved Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Energy Management Strategy for Hybrid Electric Agricultural Tractor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Current hybrid tractors predominantly employ traditional rules-based energy management strategy, which can be inefficient and heavily reliant on professional expertise. Additionally, the working cycle for these tractors mainly utilizes the existing vehicle road cycle, which is inadequate in meeting the working conditions of tractors, thereby resulting in the underutilization of hybrid tractors for their energy-saving potential. In this paper, a novel tractor working cycle is constructed, which takes into consideration the power take-off mechanism of the hybrid tractor and is, therefore, more compatible with tractor working conditions. Moreover, an improved deep reinforcement learning-based energy management strategy is proposed, named softmax deep deterministic policy gradient, based on the newly constructed working cycle to avoid inefficient searching, thereby enhancing the algorithm’s efficiency.

articleTitle: Model for Quantifying Reliability Contribution of Distribution System with Distributed Generation Based on Shapley Value
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In the power system, power outages are usually caused by the distribution system. Therefore, it is necessary to allocate the system reliability indexes to each component, so as to identify the components that have great influence on the system reliability, and to optimize them in order to improve the system reliability. In this paper, firstly, multi-state output power model of distributed generation is established, using historical distributed generation data. Then, based on Shapley value, the system reliability indexes are allocated to each component, and by standardizing them, the contribution rate of each component to the system index can be obtained. Finally, a distribution system for RBTS Bus 6 is introduced as standard case to demonstrate the validity of the proposed method. By analyzing the calculation results, it can be obtained that the component contribution rate is related to the size of the component reliability parameters and the location of the component.

articleTitle: Self-responsive Frequency Control Strategy for Electrical Energy Storage Based on Set Action Thresholds
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The rapid increase in the proportion of new energy access to the grid has led to the problem of insufficient primary FM (frequency modulation) capacity of the power system becoming more and more prominent, and the safe and stable operation of the system frequency is facing challenges. The rapid development of electric energy storage provides a new opportunity for system frequency regulation, and the use of electric energy storage charging/discharging dual fast control characteristics of the system frequency regulation control will play an important role in improving the system frequency stability. To this end, this paper proposes a self-responsive frequency control strategy based on the set action threshold of electric energy storage. Firstly, the mechanism of using the two-way power control of electric energy storage to participate in the system frequency regulation is described; based on this, the electric energy storage frequency regulation control model is established; for the characteristics of the system frequency rapid change, the study sets the self-response frequency control action threshold, and puts forward the electric energy storage self-response frequency control strategy based on the setting of the action threshold; finally, the validity of the proposed strategy and the advantages of the regulation are verified through the analysis of the calculation example.

articleTitle: Whole Life Cycle Cost Assessment of Reconfigurable Battery Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Battery energy storage can promote renewable energy consumption, reduce the frequency fluctuation of the power grid, maintain the balance of supply and demand, and ensure the safe, stable and reliable operation of the system, but with the continuous expansion of the scale of energy storage, the cost has become an important factor restricting the large-scale promotion of energy storage, so it is necessary to study the economics of the energy storage system. First, a reconfigurable coupling topology is designed to overcome the problem of low flexibility and fault tolerance of the traditional fixed series-parallel structure; second, based on this topology, the costs of the battery energy storage system in the whole life cycle are refined by taking into account the impacts of the project cycle and the energy storage lifecycle on the value, and the corresponding mathematical model is established for each cost; At the same time, in order to visualize the cost advantage of the battery energy storage system, the levelized cost model is used to evaluate the energy storage system, and the existing levelized cost model is improved by combining the characteristics of the energy storage project; finally, the levelized cost of the battery energy storage system is calculated by combining with the specific cases, and the cost competitiveness of the battery energy storage system is evaluated.

articleTitle: Contract Decision-Making Model of Load Aggregator Considering Response Uncertainty of Small and Medium-Sized Users
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In the electricity market environment, the uncertainty of user response behavior has a significant impact on demand response implementers. As a professional demand response resource aggregation and authorization agency, Load Aggregators (LA) pay more attention to contract optimization that takes into account the randomness of their returns. Decision-making problem, therefore a LA contract decision-making model based on considering user response uncertainty is proposed. This model reflects the impact of uncertainty in user response behavior on decision-making results through LA operating mechanism and cost-benefit analysis, and introduces Markov chain speculation and Monte Carlo simulation to solve the impact of uncertainty factors in the contract decision-making model, a decision-making model was proposed. Finally, taking LA that aggregates small and medium-sized users as an example, the profit indicators and contract decision quantities in the decision-making process are simulated based on the decision-maker’s decision-making preferences, which verifies the effectiveness and practical value of the contract decision-making analysis method proposed in this article.

articleTitle: A Novel Data Enhancement Method for Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Considering Spatio-Temporal Features Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Newly established Photovoltaic (PV) plants usually face the problem of lack of data, resulting in low accuracy of PV power prediction due to insufficient training data. An effective way to solve this problem is data enhancement, which expands the PV dataset so that the PV forecasting model has sufficient training data. However, conventional data enhancement methods typically focus on temporal characteristics of PV data, neglecting spatial aspects among PV power stations, resulting in poor quality of generated PV data. Accordingly, this paper introduces a data enhancement method for PV based on spatio-temporal feature extraction. Initially, temporal and spatial features of PV power station data are extracted using improved autoencoder combined with graph convolutional network. Subsequently, a density-based clustering method with noise is employed to categorize PV power stations with analogous spatio-temporal features. For PV sites with insufficient data, data from their similar stations, and data generated through the conditional adversarial generation network, are used as two types of expanded data, respectively. Ultimately, the efficient fusion of these two types of data is achieved using XGBoost to get the final enhanced PV data. Finally, Data from real PV plants are used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed data enhancement method.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Test of HVDC Control and Protection Device Based on ADPSS Self-Developed Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The closed-loop test of HVDC control and protection device is an experimental research work carried out by connecting the power system real-time digital simulation device to the HVDC control and protection device. Its main function is to verify the effectiveness of the control and protection strategy, investigate the potential problems and hidden dangers in the control and protection device, and then accurately simulate the operation characteristics of the HVDC transmission project through the digital-analog hybrid simulation in the simulation of the large power grid, so as to ensure the safe, stable and efficient operation of the power grid. Interface technology is the key technology to realize the closed-loop test of HVDC control and protection device. This paper introduces the closed-loop test technology of HVDC control and protection device based on ADPSS self-developed interface, and develops the optical protocol conversion interface device and physical interface device. Based on this interface technology, the closed-loop test of Qingyu UHVDC transmission project is carried out, and the effectiveness of ADPSS self-developed interface is verified. The interface device developed in this paper can completely replace the foreign interface device by function, and overcome the "bottleneck" technology of the long-term restriction in the interface of the power system digital-analog hybrid simulation field, which can realize the nationalized customization of the closed-loop test scheme for the HVDC control and protection device.

articleTitle: Optimization and Scheduling Method for the Operation of Hydrogen-Thermal-Electric Multi-Energy Flow Microgrid System Considering Uncertainty in New Energy Vehicle Load Demand
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: To ensure the stable operation of the hydrogen-electric-thermal multi-energy flow system under the impact of New Energy Vehicle (NEV) loads and to improve the system's economic efficiency, this paper proposes an optimization and scheduling method for the operation of the hydrogen-electric-thermal multi-energy flow microgrid system considering the uncertainty of NEV load demand. Firstly, a simulation prediction model for NEV loads and a model for the hydrogen-electric-thermal multi-energy flow microgrid system are established. Secondly, an optimization model for scheduling is established with the system's economic benefits as the objective function, taking into account the NEV load. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified using the MATLAB platform. The results indicate that this optimization method effectively meets the real-time load demand of the system and reduces the impact of loads on the grid. Compared to dispatch based solely on fixed energy supply plans, this optimization method reduces electricity purchased from the grid, decreases reliance on the main grid, and improves the system's energy utilization efficiency by approximately 7%. Although operational costs may slightly increase, the overall economic benefits are better.

articleTitle: Research on the Mechanism of Electric Vehicle Aggregators Participating in Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The current ownership of Electric Vehicles (EVs) in China is experiencing rapid growth, which presents new challenges to the distribution of electric grid loads. At present, the pricing strategies and demand response mechanisms of EV charging aggregators are of great practical importance, as they guide EV users to charge their vehicles during off-peak hours and alleviate the grid load during peak hours. This paper presents a leader-follower game model in which the aggregator, acting as the leader, sets electricity prices to encourage EV users to charge during off-peak periods, thereby reducing the pressure on the electricity supply during peak periods. In addition, a mixed integer linear programming method is employed to solve the model, ensuring global optimality of the strategy. Empirical evidence indicates that electricity prices should be adaptively adjusted in accordance with seasonal fluctuations and changes in demand in order to maximize the aggregator's revenue and minimize the user's charging costs. This approach is conducive to the deployment of electric vehicles and the advancement of smart grids.

articleTitle: Trading Mechanism of Cross-Regional Green Electricity Considering Carbon Emission Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In this paper, a cross-regional green electricity trading mechanism addresses the problem of unbalanced supply and demand due to different renewable energy situations in different regions. At the same time, considering the problem of global warming, increasing environmental pollution and avoiding excessive carbon emissions when only considering trading, the carbon emission trading is considered in this mechanism. A renewable energy-rich region is chosen as an example, and the constraints of the carbon emission market and renewable energy quota are used to optimize the dispatch with the objective function of minimizing the daily operating cost. The results of the calculation example prove that the trading mechanism of crossregional green electricity considering carbon emission trading reduces the operating cost of the responsible entity by CNY 2986072 and improves the utilization rate of renewable energy by 18.46% compared to no cross-regional green electricity trading.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis Method for Dry Reactor Based on RIME-SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Dry hollow reactor occupies an important position in the power system, and its fault diagnosis is a prerequisite to ensure the safe and stable operation of the power system. The traditional dry reactor fault diagnosis methods have problems such as low accuracy and easy to fall into the local optimal solution. In view of the above problems, this paper proposes a dry reactor turn-to-turn fault diagnosis method based on the frost algorithm (RIME) SVM algorithm. For the initial turn-to-turn short-circuit fault identification and diagnosis of dry-type hollow reactor, firstly, the turn-to-turn short-circuit fault characteristics are analyzed and the fault diagnosis features are selected. Then, combined with the global convergence and stability of RIME, the dry reactor fault diagnosis is realized by using RIME optimized SVM. Simulation results show that the RIME algorithm can quickly and efficiently realize the optimization of SVM parameters, and can jump out of the problem of local optimization. The model proposed in this paper has higher recognition accuracy and faster convergence, and can better recognize dry reactor turn-to-turn faults.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Storage Configuration for Park and Ride (P+R) Charging Stations with Regenerative Braking Energy in Urban Rail Transit
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Rail transit energy storage technology not only enables the large-scale absorption of regenerative braking energy from trains, increasing the system's energy utilization efficiency but also offers energy support to new types of loads, such as electric vehicle charging stations. This study focuses on the research of energy storage capacity optimization for rail transit- P+R electric vehicle charging stations. Based on the operational characteristics of rail transit and electric vehicles, an optimization model for rail transit-electric vehicle charging station configuration is developed to obtain the optimal storage capacity. Simultaneously, the study analyzes the differences in economic indicators such as configuration capacity and investment costs for various types of energy storage devices. It delves into the impact of different factors on the optimal energy storage configuration.

articleTitle: Stability Control Strategy of Photovoltaic DC Microgrid System based on Distributed Hydrogen Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In response to the issue of energy supply instability that arises from the widespread adoption of distributed renewable energy resources at the user-end in the future, a DC microgrid system and control method based on distributed hydrogen energy storage are presented. Firstly, the mathematical models of photovoltaic power generation, electrochemical energy storage, and electrolyzer-hydrogen storage tank-fuel cell hydrogen energy storage system are established. Secondly, the components are coupled to establish an integrated DC microgrid system. Finally, based on the control objective of DC bus voltage stabilization, the corresponding control strategy is proposed. According to different fluctuation situations, the effects on the system and the effectiveness of the control strategy are analyzed when the input or load fluctuate.

articleTitle: Integrated Supply Allocation Strategy for Power System in Emergency
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Due to the high dependence of modern society on electricity supplies and the increasing complexity of power systems, the interruption risk in power supply caused by sudden events such as natural disasters and human accidents has a significant impact on critical infrastructure, public services, and social stability. Therefore, establishing an emergency power system supplies allocation mechanism is highly necessary. This paper proposes an integrated supply allocation strategy, which first establishes a grey prediction model to analyze the necessity of supply allocation. Secondly, it utilizes the K-medoids algorithm to establish a clustering model, combines it with a multi-level grey comprehensive evaluation model to optimize the modeling of allocation point quantity, and obtains an optimal site using immune optimization algorithms, successfully predicting the optimal number and locations for site selection. Subsequently, an Auto Regressive Moving Average (ARMA) model algorithm is employed to establish to predict the distribution solutions for resource allocation. Finally, the optimized distribution path is obtained by Heuristic Particle Swarm Optimization (HPSO) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy greatly improves the efficiency of emergencies allocation through the optimal distribution sites and path planning, significantly reducing the negative effects caused by abrupt accidents.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Distributed Dispatch for Integrated Electricity and Heat Systems: A Multi-agent PPO Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Considering that energy suppliers within the Integrated Electricity and Heat System (IEHS) typically provide only partial information to other suppliers for privacy protection, traditional centralized scheduling methods are no longer applicable. This paper proposes a method based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning to address the distributed dispatch problem within the IEHS. To transform the optimization problem of the IEHS into a reinforcement learning model in a multi-agent environment, the IEHS is divided according to different stakeholders into electrical system agents and heat system agents, thereby establishing a partially observable Markov decision process. Subsequently, the multi-agent proximal policy optimization algorithm is utilized to solve this problem, creating a training and solution framework suitable for the IEHS that supports centralized training and decentralized execution.

articleTitle: Preventive Control Methods for Power Systems Based on Improved Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Convergence speed, accuracy, generalization and decision transparency are very important indices for transient stability preventive control generation methods based on AI. This paper proposes a transient stability preventive control generation method based on graph deep reinforcement learning and its interpretation method using mutual information optimization. Firstly, a transient stability preventive control generation model is built based on the framework of deep reinforcement learning algorithm. The grid domain buses are mapped to the graph domain nodes and the grid graph data samples are generated. The graph convolutional neural network via initial residual and identity mapping (GCNII) is used to build the action network and the evaluation network. Secondly, based on the GCNII network, a transient stability assessment model is built and pre-trained, and graph data samples containing varies of topological structures and power flow states are applied to train the model. Then the interpretation method based on mutual information optimization is used to analyze the decision-making basis of the transient stability assessment model. The dominant factor affecting the transient instability of power system is extracted and its contribution degree is quantified, and the abduction analysis of transient stability is realized. Finally, the pre-trained transient stability assessment model is embedded in the deep reinforcement learning framework as a guide, and the power flow adjustment method is used to preferentially correct the weak factors and their influencing factors so that the transient stability prevention control strategies are obtained. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified in the IEEE-39 node test system.

articleTitle: Elastic Configuration Method of New Energy and Storage for Rail Transit Green Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Under the joint guidance of the "carbon peaking and carbon neutrality" strategy and the "a country with strong transportation network" strategy, it has become an effective means to implement the above strategy to connect the traction power supply system with new energy and energy storage equipment to form a rail transit green energy system. However, how to make good use of new energy and energy storage equipment, so that it can provide emergency power supply in time in the case of short-term power loss in the traction power supply network, and reduce the impact of power loss on the system, is still in the initial stage of research. Aiming at the problem that there is a time difference between the traditional emergency power supply (such as diesel generator) and the traction power supply network to provide backup power, an emergency planning model is established. Firstly, the constant power model of photovoltaic output and the equivalent model of traction load are constructed. Then, according to the actual situation, the planning configuration model under emergency conditions is constructed. Finally, the configuration results are analyzed. The results show that the proposed model can fully consider the actual situation of the station, give full play to the emergency efficiency, and provide a feasible scheme for improving the elasticity of the traction power supply system.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation Strategy of Multi-energy Coupled Microgrids Considering Carbon Trading and Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Under the environmental degradation and energy crisis, energy conservation and emission reduction has become a broad consensus of the community. In this context, the multi-energy coupled microgrids is one of the key means to achieve the goal of " low carbon, " which can effectively solve the low efficiency of social energy utilization and the failure of large-scale application of renewable energy. Firstly, this paper constructs a model on the demand side, and divides the demand response into two types: price type and substitution type. Based on the peak-valley electricity price theory, an electrothermal price demand response model is established under the demand response mechanism. The carbon trading mechanism is introduced into the multi-energy coupled microgrids and combined with demand response. The conclusion of this paper shows that the demand response mechanism and the carbon trading mechanism can complement each other and work together to achieve the low-carbon economic operation of the system. This can provide useful experience for future energy management decisions, especially for the planning and design of multi-energy complementary systems. At the same time, it provides relevant ideas and methods for how to consider renewable energy and carbon trading mechanisms in the planning and design process.

articleTitle: Research on the Potential Evaluation of Load Regulation for Commercial Building Users Based on FAHP and Improved Entropy Weighting
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Harnessing load control potential plays a crucial role in improving system reliability and promoting renewable energy integration in commercial building power systems. With the development of the economy and industry, the demand for power load in commercial buildings is increasing, further increasing the difference between peak and off-peak electricity demand. To ensure the security of power supply in commercial buildings and system stability, it is necessary to evaluate the adjustable load potential in these buildings. Existing research often overlooks the influence of subjective factors such as user preferences and user cooperation on load control potential, leading to biased evaluation results. Regarding quantitative evaluation methods, the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) is commonly used, but it suffers from subjectivity. Therefore, it is necessary to incorporate the objective weighting method in load control potential assessment. In this study, a combination of Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) and Improved Entropy Weighting Method is used to select and quantify key indicators as variables for constructing a load forecasting potential assessment model. Based on this, an evaluation model is established from the perspectives of load, economy, users, and management to quantify the load control potential. Finally, a fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method is applied to assess the load control potential in commercial buildings. The case analysis demonstrates that the indicator system and evaluation method are reasonable. The evaluation method and model are effective and practical in exploring the load control potential in commercial buildings, providing a reliable basis for demand response in grid supply-demand balance regulation. Exploring load control potential is of great significance in altering the load curve of commercial users and achieving peak shaving and valley filling in the power grid.

articleTitle: A Fault Blocking Method for Distribution Network Based on Offline Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The fault outage time caused by the distribution network accounts for 80% of the total outage time. Due to the access of a large number of distributed power sources, it is easy to cause cascading failures and large-scale power outages after the failure occurs. This paper proposes a fault blocking method for distribution network based on offline reinforcement learning. The proposed method does not need to interact with the real distribution network nor does it need to accurately model the distribution network. Only historical data is needed to obtain a feasible distribution network fault blocking strategy through offline reinforcement learning methods. The IEEE 16 node distribution network system is used to verify the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method reduces the average fault recovery time by 8.5% and the network loss by 6.7%, outperforming previous reinforcement learning methods.

articleTitle: Distribution Defense Hardening Against Typhoon Disasters Considering Decision-Dependent Uncertainty and Optimal Restoration Schedule
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Distribution Defense Hardening (DDH) is an effective measure to reduce the economic losses caused by natural disasters such as typhoons. However, previous works have neglected the coupling between the line reinforcement decision and the optimal restoration scheduling of maintenance teams. This paper presents an integrated framework to improve the resilience of distribution networks to typhoon disasters. Firstly, Monte Carlo sampling method was used to simulate and quantify the spatio-temporal state of the distribution network under typhoon disaster. DDU reflects the impact of enhanced decision-making on distribution lines, and its modeling was integrated into the scenario simulation to solve it. Then, the scenario simulation was integrated into the proposed two-stage Stochastic Mixed Integer Programming (SMIP) model. The order of magnitude of line reinforcement decisions results in high computational complexity. Therefore, the Sample Average Approximation (SAA) algorithm was introduced to solve this problem. Finally, the proposed framework and its solution algorithm are validated on an IEEE 33-node system. The significant cost savings and resilience improvement demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Integration of Knowledge Graph and Power Grid Knowledge for Equipment Data Compliance Discrimination in Low-Voltage Distribution Area
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: This paper proposes a compliance discrimination method for low-voltage distribution network equipment that integrates knowledge graph and power grid knowledge, improving the efficiency of data governance for low-voltage distribution network equipment and providing assurance for data governance and data quality improvement of equipment. This method first collects multi-source data from the low-pressure distribution area, and then processes the data through text processing, neural network and other methods to form a standardized graph database. Then Neo4j is used to construct the knowledge graph. On this basis, according to the various rules existing in the low-voltage distribution area, the conformance check of the equipment's own attributes and the upstream and downstream relationships is carried out, so as to identify the non-compliance data in the knowledge graph.

articleTitle: Wind Power Prediction based on Potts Model Feature Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the development of new energy, the wind power prediction problem has been a popular research direction. Most of the forecasting models only focus on the relationship between variables and the forecasting series, ignoring the complex interactions between wind power variables and the autocorrelation in time. We propose a new time-series predictor-variable optimization method, PMFO (Potts Model Feature Optimization), in conjunction with the Potts model in classical aerodynamics, and combine it with the BERT model in the neural network approach to obtain more accurate predictions. First, the aerodynamic field of the Potts model is analyzed as an excitation model for the feature planning of wind power generation variables. In this model, we treat the time series of wind generation variables as a kind of path sum of infinitesimal trajectory increments, where each infinitesimal increment is controlled by the Potts gas model. This is followed by a modified input layer into a BERT network for power prediction to obtain the results. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of the method with a real power grid dataset, and also embed the method into other neural network models, all of which show varying degrees of performance improvement, demonstrating the excellence of the method in this paper.

articleTitle: An Alternating Direction Method Based on Hypersphere Sampling for Robust Look-Ahead Power Dispatch Using Ellipsoidal Uncertainty Set
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In look-ahead power dispatch, the incorporation of a Two-Stage Robust Optimization (TSRO) approach is an effective method for addressing the uncertainties associated with large-scale wind power integration. However, when employing an ellipsoidal uncertainty set that captures the correlations more accurately, solving the TSRO problem becomes challenging. To address this issue, this paper introduces an alternating direction method based on hypersphere sampling. The proposed method leverages the unique representation of the ellipsoid to project sampling points from the hypersphere onto the corresponding ellipsoidal surface, thereby resolving the difficulty in selecting initial values when using an ellipsoidal uncertainty set. The case study compares the proposed method with the exact KarushKuhn‒Tucker approach, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method and significantly highlighting its advantages in convergence efficiency.

articleTitle: Fault Disposal Plan Generation Technology under Distribution Network Maintenance Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: During distribution network maintenance and operation inspections, it is common to have prior knowledge data such as maintenance schedules, rules and regulations, maintenance history records, and operation plans. Utilize the above knowledge to introduce human-machine collaborative knowledge enhancement technology into the machine intelligence of distribution network operation decision-making. This will ensure that the entire process of machine intelligence training and decision-making is guided by human knowledge. By using machine intelligence to analyze the maintenance status of the distribution network, the operation mode under maintenance can ensure the reliability of the power supply. Realize proactive risk detection and tracking, provide support for decision-making assistance, quickly respond to power grid emergencies and unplanned maintenance, and ensure the safe and stable operation of the power grid. The verification and compilation of maintenance operation modes can also be enhanced through human-machine collaborative data knowledge, continuously optimizing compilation behavior based on expert feedback, and conducting independent updates and learning to gradually adapt to the needs of expert verification and scheduling under the "two-carbon" situation, and even changes in power grid operation goals. As a result, the practicality of the agent backup module for the maintenance and operation mode of the distribution system has been improved, supporting the level of auxiliary decision-making.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Objective Coordinated Scheduling Optimization of Microgrids Considering Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: To effectively enhance the renewable energy optimal allocation capabilities of microgrids and reduce the impact of new energy uncertainties, this paper proposes a multi-objective coordinated scheduling optimization model for microgrids that considers the uncertainty of new energy sources. Firstly, by integrating the Graph Convolutional Network (Graph Convolutional Network, GUN) with the Gated Recurrent Unit (gated recurrent unit, GRU), a spatiotemporal graph convolutional neural network is established, which leverages the advantages of graph convolution in extracting spatial features and the strengths of gated recurrent units in capturing temporal features, thereby deeply exploring the hidden spatiotemporal dependencies among photovoltaic stations. Secondly, a two-stage rolling scheduling optimization model for microgrids is developed, followed by the application of the Column-and-Constraint Generation (C&CG) algorithm, which decomposes the two-stage optimization model into master and sub-problems for iterative interaction and solution. Finally, the effectiveness and economic benefits of the proposed methods are validated through case study analysis.

articleTitle: Coordinated Emergency Frequency Control Strategy for Diverse Heterogeneous Resources in the Receiving-End Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: To cope with low-frequency issues in the receiverend power grid during large power deficit accidents, a coordinated emergency frequency control strategy utilizing multiple heterogeneous resources is proposed. Firstly, a frequency response model considers the characteristics of various heterogeneous resources, including renewable energy units, battery energy storage system, pumped hydro storage, high-voltage direct current and interruptible loads, is built considering different scenarios. Then, an emergency frequency control model is established, aiming to minimize the cost of frequency regulation under disturbances while considering operational security constraints. This model involves the participation of multiple heterogeneous resources in a coordinated manner. By solving the emergency frequency control model with the participation of multiple heterogeneous resources, the output levels of each resource and the required amount of load shedding for frequency stability control are determined. After optimization, a coordinated frequency emergency control scheme is obtained, utilizing multiple heterogeneous resources. Finally, case studies using a modified IEEE RTS-79 system demonstrate that the proposed emergency control strategy ensures transient frequency compliance with security requirements under major disturbances in the receiver-end power grid. It significantly reduces the required amount of load shedding for stability control and minimizes the cost of frequency regulation.

articleTitle: Cooperative Self-response Control Strategy of Electric Energy Storage and SVG Based on Transient Overvoltage Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Large-scale new energy is an important part of new energy consumption through long-distance transmission of UHVDC. However, when a bipolar blocking fault occurs in UHVDC, it will cause a large surge of transient voltage in the AC power grid at the DC sending end, which seriously affects the safe operation of the AC power grid at the DC sending end. Although the DC feeder grid has been put into operation with large-capacity energy storage plant and SVG, the control of transient over-voltage still fails to achieve the desired effect. For this reason, this paper firstly analyzes the transient over-voltage caused by double-pole blocking of UHVDC feeder AC grid, studies the response control characteristics of electric energy storage and SVG to the transient voltage; sets up the self-response synergistic threshold of electric energy storage and SVG to cope with the transient over-voltage, and based on this, puts forward the self-response synergistic control strategy of electric energy storage and SVG to cope with the transient over-voltage; and finally, verifies the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy in this paper by simulation. Finally, simulation verifies the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Load Modeling Method for Distribution Networks Considering Electric Vehicle V2G
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the global popularity of Electric Vehicles (EVs), accurate modeling and prediction of their impact on the power system are crucial. On the basis of research on the universal equivalent model of EV charging load, a generalized comprehensive load model for distribution networks considering the V2G (vehicle to grid) characteristics of EVs is proposed. The proposed model not only takes into accounts the characteristics of an EV as power load, but also covers its potential as a power source, i.e., V2G technology that allows EVs to deliver energy to the grid when needed. The validity of the model is verified through simulation analysis in the Simulink/Matlab environment, accurately reflecting the impact of EV charging and V2G operations on the distribution network. This study provides strong support for grid load forecasting and management, and offers a new perspective for the combined development of EVs and smart grids. By considering the "source" and "load" dual-characteristics of EVs, the model proposed in this paper is expected to help power system operators optimize grid operation and enhance the adaptability and resilience of the grid to the large-scale integration of EVs.

articleTitle: Research on Key Parameter Identification of New Energy Units Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: The large-scale access of new energy leads to more complex stability of the power grid, and it is urgent to improve the accuracy of the new energy unit modeling for system stability simulation analysis. There are many types of new energy units and the control parameters are difficult to obtain directly, which makes it difficult to accurately construct the system stability analysis model. Therefore, a parameter identification method based on improved genetic algorithm is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the module analysis model is established to identify the key control parameters. Then, the parameter space discretization method is used for pre-screening to narrow the parameter identification range and reduce the convergence time. The iterative calculation is carried out according to the improved genetic algorithm, and then the output results are optimized by regression search and variable domain search, so as to reduce the error. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed identification method is verified through case analysis.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Performance Evaluation Method for Flywheel Array Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Flywheel energy storage, characterized by high power and fast response, is an effective means to meet the short-term and high-frequency regulation needs of power systems. Accurate assessment of flywheel performance is of great significance in ensuring stable operation of power systems and promoting technological progress. However, limited by the development of technology, capacity and other parameters of flywheel are insufficient, usually unable to meet the regulatory requirements, so it is necessary to use multiple flywheels to form Flywheel Array Energy Storage System (FAESS). FAESS needs to coordinate the action of each flywheel unit, build the array topology, design communication and control systems, so that its output characteristics differ from the individual flywheel. Therefore, research on the performance evaluation method of flywheel arrays is needed. In this paper, we introduce the current research status of flywheel energy storage evaluation indicator system, then analyze the current topology structure of flywheel array and its communication system. Finally, we propose a flywheel array evaluation indicator system that considers the influence of array aggregation topology, providing reference for the performance evaluation and optimization design of FAESS.

articleTitle: Investigation on Policies and Projects Related to the Development of Novel Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: This article presents an investigation into the development, policies, and projects of novel energy storage. Initially, we provided an overview of energy planning and industry policies related to energy storage in typical countries including the United States, Australia, and China. Subsequently, we analyzed the characteristics, operational modes, and participation of three lithium-ion battery-based electrochemical energy storage projects in electricity markets. Finally, based on our analysis, we proposed suggestions and future prospects for the advancement of novel energy storage technologies. Our findings aim to offer valuable insights and guidance for the further promotion and application of these technologies.

articleTitle: Optimization Operation Strategy For New Energy Microgrids Considering The Impact Of Tiered Carbon Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the gradual depletion of fossil fuels and the intensification of environmental pollution in recent years, the development of clean and environmentally friendly new energy is the trend. The emergence of microgrids provides new choices for integrating diverse forms of renewable energy. Microgrids can improve the utilization rate of renewable energy, improve the reliability of renewable energy supply, reduce the use of traditional fossil fuels, and reduce pollutant emissions. However, new energy microgrids with high penetration rates face difficulties in coordinated control, such as complex structures and high operating costs. Therefore, studying the economic optimization operation of new energy microgrids with high penetration rates has important theoretical significance and practical application value. This article mainly studies the optimization scheduling of microgrids under grid connection mode and adds a stepped carbon trading model to constrain the carbon emissions of microgrids, analyzing the impact of stepped carbon trading on the low-carbon and economic efficiency of microgrids.

articleTitle: The Impact Analysis of Line Inductance on System Amplitude and Frequency Stability in the Converter Interfaced System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the transition to cleaner energy sources, a high proportion of renewable devices often needs to be connected to the grid through long transmission lines, which increases the risk of system instability. The system is composed of device and network, both of which have influence on system stability. The impact of device control parameters on system stability has been widely studied, but the impact of network on system stability should not be overlooked. This paper focuses on the line inductance in the network. Firstly, it elucidates the implications of the system Amplitude and Frequency (A&F) stability, considering the dynamic characteristics of both device and the network. Secondly, it analyzes the high-order dynamic characteristics of the inherent relationship between the excitation of the amplitude/frequency of internal voltage and the response of active/reactive current, under the constraints imposed by line inductance in the network. This analysis reveals the essence of the dominant feature of this relationship, which is influenced by the system oscillation frequency. Finally, the system oscillation frequency was analyzed through closed-loop simulation, which affects the A&F stability of the system by affecting the energy storage capacity of the line inductance. This paper establishes a general understanding of the energy storage capacity of line inductor in the grid and lays the foundation for further understanding and analyzing of the mechanism of power system instability problems.

articleTitle: A Pricing Method for the Frequency Support from Battery Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Large scale integration of variable renewable energy leads to rapid reduction in inertia and frequency regulation capability, highlighting the issue of the system frequency security. As an efficient flexible regulation resource, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) have the characteristics of bidirectional power supply and flexible control, playing an increasingly important role in energy market and frequency regulation of power systems. However, it is difficult for BESS to recover costs solely through price arbitrage. Encouraging them to provide frequency support through economic means can ensure system frequency security and promote BESS profitability. It is crucial to price the frequency support BESS reasonably. This paper establishes a mathematical model for BESS to provide virtual inertial and Fast Frequency Response (FFR). It is incorporated into a security constrained economic scheduling model coupled with the energy market. This paper considers dynamic frequency safety and price the virtual inertia and FFR through dual operation after second-order cone linearization of the minimum frequency constraint. Case study shows that the proposed pricing method can fairly quantify the inertia and frequency response with different performances. Compared to pricing based on SCUC, pricing based on SCED can accurately reflect the system's demand for virtual inertia and fast frequency response.

articleTitle: Design of Tiered Capacity Market Mechanism with Generation and Consumer Participation in China
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid growth of renewable energy power generation and the rising proportion of installed capacity have introduced new difficulties and challenges to the regulatory capacity of the power system. The capacity market represents a crucial component of the mature electricity market system. It ensures the return on the power system regulatory resources and plays a significant role in maintaining the long-term abundance of generating capacity. The paper collates the existing capacity guarantee mechanisms at home and abroad, and analyze the development mode of the capacity mechanism suitable for the actual conditions in China. The research innovatively designs a capacity market mechanism that engages market participants on both sides of power generation and utilization. It also elaborates on the key aspects of declaration, clearing, and settlement. Additionally, the proposal suggests the establishment of a tiered capacity market in the context of the rapidly increasing number of small market participants, such as distributed power sources. The articulation mechanism of different tiers of capacity market is clarified, with the intention of providing useful reference for the construction of the capacity market in China.

articleTitle: Tri-stage Modeling of Urban-level Electrical-Water Fault Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Multi-voltage-level urban power network (UPN) is the basis for other infrastructure networks, especially water distribution network (WDN). Compared with other networks, UPN is more vulnerable to extreme events, including extreme weather events and deliberate attacks. The affection of UPN fault on WDN displays complex multi-stage characteristics. This paper first proposes a comprehensive tri-stage model of electrical-water fault propagation, including the electrical-water network connection model, the reduced-order hydraulic network model, and the water supply model of customers. Second, a scenario selection method is proposed. Finally, the proposed model is verified by a simplified real-world urban power and water network based on the selected typical fault scenarios.

articleTitle: Cluster Power Prediction Considering Spatio-Temporal Correlation Characteristics of Distributed Photovoltaic Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the rapid spread of distributed PV power systems, accurate power prediction has become a critical requirement to ensure grid stability and optimise energy dispatch. Compared with the power prediction of individual PV power plants, distributed PV cluster prediction is more challenging. In order to improve the accuracy of distributed PV cluster power prediction, this paper considers the spatio-temporal correlation between distributed PV stations and proposes a method of distributed PV cluster power prediction based on representative stations selection and Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (STGCN). Firstly, the representative station is selected by using the integrated correlation coefficient as an evaluation index through the principle of maximum correlation-minimum redundancy. Then the weight of each representative power station is calculated using the Secretary Bird Optimisation Algorithm (SBOA). STGCN is used to predict the power of PV power plants considering spatial correlation, and finally the cluster predicted power will be obtained. Eventually, example calculations are carried out in two PV clusters in Jilin Province and Hebei Province to prove the effectiveness of this paper's method in cluster prediction.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Scheduling Strategy Considering Multi-Time Scale Air Conditioning Load Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: With the widespread integration of distributed renewable energy, energy storage technologies, and demand-side resources, power grid operation faces unprecedented challenges and transformations. This paper proposes a multi-time scale schedule strategy for air conditioning load demand response, optimizing distribution network operations by coordinating price-based and incentive-based demand responses across different time scales. A simulation study using the IEEE 33-node distribution network system validates the proposed scheme's effectiveness in reducing load loss and lowering system operating costs. By comparing three schedule schemes, results indicate that the multi-time scale strategy, which involves Energy Storage Systems (ESS) and Air Conditioning Load Aggregators (ACLA), significantly reduces load shedding and economic losses, thereby enhancing the stability and efficiency of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Modeling of Inter-Regional Renewable Power Trading Capacity Considering Generation and Load Fluctuation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Power and Energy Technology (ICPET)
abstract: Inter-regional electricity trading is vital to promote the integration of renewable generation. It is critical to accurately estimate the power exchange capability for the different regions to participate in the inter-regional electricity market. To address the impacts of generation and load fluctuation, this paper proposes a stochastic fuzzy method to model the uncertainty of inter-regional power exchange capability. First, the conditional probability distribution of renewable power generation under different prediction levels is studied based on Copula theory, and the impact of local consumption fluctuations is considered to correct the model. Then, a stochastic fuzzy model is developed to integrate meteorology forecast information and impacts of consumption fluctuation. Case studies based on real-world data validate the superiority of the proposed method against existing models.
